translations.fa: عاشقشه. بابا هم با من همین‌طور بود. حالا قلبشه — دکتر می‌گه داره ضعیف میشه. هفتاد و شش سالشه.

branches.suggestion: I'm so sorry, Tom. How is he coping?
branches.suggestionFa: خیلی متأسفم تام. چطور کنار میاد؟

branches.suggestion: That must be really hard for all of you.

n6.speaker: tom
n6.text: Stubborn as ever. Some mornings I still wave at the depot like he's in the cab. Daft, eh?

translations.fa: مثل همیشه یک‌دنده. بعضی صبح‌ها هنوز به پایانه دست تکون می‌دم انگار تو کابینه. احمقانه‌ست، نه؟

branches.suggestion: It's not daft at all.
In my culture, we talk to our loved ones too.
branches.suggestionFa: تو فرهنگ من، ما هم با عزیزانمون حرف می‌زنیم.

n7.speaker: tom
n7.text: Yeah? That's nice, that. You lost someone too, didn't you? You don't have to say.

translations.fa: آره؟ قشنگه این. تو هم کسی را از دست دادی، نه؟ لازم نیست بگی.

branches.suggestion: My grandfather. I couldn't go to his funeral.
I'd rather not talk about it yet, if that's okay.
branches.suggestionFa: ترجیح می‌دم فعلاً دربارش حرف نزنم، اگه اشکالی نداره.

cultureNote.en: British people often give space with "You don't have to say" — it's an invitation, not a demand.
cultureNote.fa: این جمله دعوت است، نه اجبار.

n8.speaker: tom
n8.text: That's alright, mate. Whenever you're ready. The garden's always here, and so's the kettle.

translations.fa: اشکالی نداره رفیق. هر وقت آماده بودی. باغچه همیشه اینجاست، کتری هم همین‌طور.

branches.suggestion: Thank you, Tom. That means a lot.
branches.suggestionFa: ممنون تام. خیلی برام ارزش داره.

branches.suggestion: Your dad must be so proud of the man you are.
branches.suggestionFa: بابات حتماً به مردی که هستی افتخار می‌کنه.

n9.speaker: tom
n9.text: Cheers, mate. You're family now — that's why I told you. Come on — Dad'll want his tea, and Leslie'll think we've run off.

translations.fa: مرسی رفیق. الان جزو خانواده‌ای — برای همین بهت گفتم. بیا — بابا چاییش را می‌خواد، و لزلی فکر می‌کنه فرار کردیم.

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: These are Tom's letters from when we were nineteen. He wrote one every day for a summer. Don't tell him I kept them!

translations.fa: اینا نامه‌های تامه از وقتی نوزده سالمون بود. یه تابستون هر روز یکی نوشت. بهش نگی نگهشون داشتم!

branches.suggestion: That's so sweet — your secret's safe with me.
branches.suggestionFa: خیلی شیرینه — رازت پیش من محفوظه.

branches.suggestion: Every day? Where were you that summer?
branches.suggestionFa: هر روز؟ اون تابستون کجا بودی؟

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: I was working at a holiday camp in Skegness. He was stuck in London, driving his dad's bus routes on Saturdays.

translations.fa: تو یه اردوگاه تعطیلات تو اسکگنس کار می‌کردم. اون تو لندن گیر بود، شنبه‌ها مسیرهای اتوبوس باباش را می‌روند.

branches.suggestion: A holiday camp? That sounds fun.
branches.suggestionFa: اردوگاه تعطیلات؟ باحال به نظر میاد.

branches.suggestion: So it was a long-distance relationship!
branches.suggestionFa: پس یه رابطهٔ از راه دور بود!

cultureNote.en: Seaside holiday camps like Butlin's were hugely popular British holidays from the 1940s onwards.
cultureNote.fa: اردوگاه‌های ساحلی تعطیلات محبوب بریتانیایی بودند.

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: Exactly. No mobiles then — just letters and the phone box on the seafront, if I had enough coins.

translations.fa: دقیقاً. اون موقع موبایل نبود — فقط نامه و باجهٔ تلفن کنار ساحل، اگه سکهٔ کافی داشتم.

branches.suggestion: I can't imagine life without a phone!
branches.suggestionFa: زندگی بدون گوشی را تصور هم نمی‌تونم!

branches.suggestion: Letters feel more romantic, though.

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: Listen to this one: "Dear Les, the 38 broke down in Islington. I thought of you the whole time." Ha!

translations.fa: گوش کن به این یکی: «لزِ عزیز، ۳۸ تو ایزلینگتون خراب شد. تمام مدت به تو فکر کردم.» ها!

branches.suggestion: That's Tom all over — romantic and practical!
branches.suggestionFa: این دقیقاً تامه — رمانتیک و عملی!

branches.suggestion: Even then he was obsessed with buses!
branches.suggestionFa: حتی اون موقع هم شیفتهٔ اتوبوس بود!

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: He was rubbish at spelling. Still is. "Beautiful" has three different spellings in here.

translations.fa: تو املا افتضاح بود. هنوزم هست. «زیبا» اینجا سه جور مختلف نوشته شده.

branches.suggestion: It's the thought that counts.
Maybe that's why you fell for him!

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: Maybe! And he always signed off "Love you more than tea".

translations.fa: شاید! و همیشه آخرش می‌نوشت «بیشتر از چای دوستت دارم».

branches.suggestion: "More than tea" — that's true love in Britain!
branches.suggestionFa: «بیشتر از چای» — این عشق واقعی تو بریتانیاست!

branches.suggestion: That's adorable. Does he still say it?

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Every anniversary. Thirty years this June. Do you write letters to anyone back home?

translations.fa: هر سالگرد. این ژوئن سی سال میشه. به کسی تو کشورت نامه می‌نویسی؟

branches.suggestion: Not letters, but I send voice notes to my mum every day.
branches.suggestionFa: نامه نه، ولی هر روز به مامانم پیام صوتی می‌فرستم.

branches.suggestion: I should. My grandmother would love a real letter.
branches.suggestionFa: باید بنویسم. مادربزرگم عاشق یه نامهٔ واقعی میشه.

n8.speaker: leslie
n8.text: Voice notes are the new letters, I suppose. Keep them — one day you'll be glad you did.

translations.fa: پیام صوتی همون نامهٔ جدیده، فکر کنم. نگهشون دار — یه روز خوشحال میشی که نگه داشتی.

branches.suggestion: I will. Thank you for sharing these with me.
branches.suggestionFa: حتماً. ممنون که اینا را با من در میون گذاشتی.

branches.suggestion: You're right. Memories are precious.

n9.speaker: leslie
n9.text: Right — box back in the attic, not a word to Tom. Fancy a cuppa? More than tea, eh?

translations.fa: خب — جعبه برگرده تو انباری، یه کلمه به تام نه. یه چای می‌چسبه؟ بیشتر از چای، ها؟

n1.speaker: patel
n1.text: Hello both, and hello Nicola! She's had a brilliant year — 'lovely ideas' in reading, and real effort in writing.

translations.fa: سلام به هر دوتون، و سلام نیکولا! سال فوق‌العاده‌ای داشته — «ایده‌های قشنگ» تو خوندن، و تلاش واقعی تو نوشتن.

branches.suggestion: That's lovely to hear — we're so proud of her.
branches.suggestionFa: شنیدنش خیلی خوبه — خیلی بهش افتخار می‌کنیم.

branches.suggestion: Thank you. She loves her reading books.

n2.speaker: patel
n2.text: Her maths is working well too. She's very good at number bonds now.

translations.fa: ریاضیش هم خوب پیش میره. الان تو ترکیب‌های عددی خیلی خوبه.

branches.suggestion: What are number bonds?
She practises adding up at home with sweets!
branches.suggestionFa: تو خونه با آب‌نبات جمع زدن تمرین می‌کنه!

cultureNote.en: "Number bonds" are pairs of numbers that make a total, like 7 + 3 = 10.
cultureNote.fa: number bonds جفت عددهایی‌اند که یک مجموع می‌سازند.

n3.speaker: patel
n3.text: Pairs of numbers that make ten, like six and four. If anything, she could put her hand up a bit more — she's quite shy in class.

translations.fa: جفت عددهایی که ده میشن، مثل شش و چهار. اگه چیزی باشه، می‌تونه یه کم بیشتر دست بلند کنه — سر کلاس نسبتاً خجالتیه.

branches.suggestion: How can we help her feel more confident at home?
branches.suggestionFa: چطور تو خونه کمکش کنیم اعتمادبه‌نفس بیشتری داشته باشه؟

branches.suggestion: Really? She never stops talking at home!
branches.suggestionFa: واقعاً؟ تو خونه یه لحظه ساکت نمی‌شه!

n4.speaker: patel
n4.text: Ask her to explain her homework to you, as if she's the teacher. Children love that.

translations.fa: ازش بخواید تکالیفش را براتون توضیح بده، انگار معلمه. بچه‌ها عاشقشن.

branches.suggestion: That's a great idea. We'll try it.
She'd love being the teacher!

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Can I show you my butterfly painting? It's on the wall!

translations.fa: می‌تونم نقاشی پروانه‌ام را نشونتون بدم؟ رو دیواره!

branches.suggestion: Yes please — I'd love to see it!
In a minute, sweetheart. Let Mrs Patel finish.
branches.suggestionFa: یه دقیقه دیگه، عزیزم. بذار خانم پاتل حرفش را تموم کنه.

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: It's this one! I used every colour. Butterflies have the same pattern on both wings.

translations.fa: این یکیه! از همه رنگ‌ها استفاده کردم. پروانه‌ها رو هر دو بالشون یه طرح دارن.

branches.suggestion: It's beautiful — the colours are amazing.
Both wings match! Very clever.
branches.suggestionFa: هر دو بال مثل همن! خیلی باهوشانه.

n7.speaker: patel
n7.text: That's called symmetry — we learned it this term. Any questions about Year 3?

translations.fa: اسمش تقارنه — این ترم یادش گرفتیم. سؤالی دربارهٔ کلاس سوم دارید؟

branches.suggestion: Who will her teacher be next year?
Will there be more homework?

cultureNote.en: In England, children start Year 1 at age five or six; Year 3 is the start of "Key Stage 2".
cultureNote.fa: سال سوم آغاز مرحلهٔ کلیدی ۲ است.

n8.speaker: patel
n8.text: Mr Ellis — he's lovely, and very calm. A little more homework, but mostly reading. Keep up the bedtime stories!

translations.fa: آقای الیس — خیلی خوبه، و خیلی آروم. یه کم تکلیف بیشتر، ولی بیشترش خوندن. قصه‌های شب را ادامه بدید!

branches.suggestion: We will. Thank you for everything this year.
branches.suggestionFa: حتماً. ممنون بابت همه چیز امسال.

branches.suggestion: Thank you, Mrs Patel. Say thank you, Nicola!
branches.suggestionFa: ممنون خانم پاتل. بگو ممنون، نیکولا!

n9.speaker: patel
n9.text: 'Well done, Nicola!' — I wrote it on the report myself. Have a lovely summer, all of you.

translations.fa: «آفرین نیکولا!» — خودم روی کارنامه نوشتمش. تابستون خوبی داشته باشید، همه‌تون.

memory.en: Mr Patel read Nicola's end-of-year report
memory.fa: آقای پاتل کارنامهٔ آخر سال نیکولا را خواند

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Hiya! I'm Nicola. What's your name?

translations.fa: سلام! من نیکولا هستم. اسمت چیه؟

branches.suggestion: My name's {you}.
Hi Nicola! I'm {you}, nice to meet you.
branches.suggestionFa: سلام نیکولا! من {you} هستم، از آشنایی‌ات خوشحالم.

cultureNote.en: "Hiya" is a friendly British hello, very common in the north and with children.
cultureNote.fa: «Hiya» یک سلام صمیمی بریتانیایی است، مخصوصاً در شمال و با بچه‌ها.

recasts.echo: Oh, your name's {you}? Lovely!

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: {you}! That's a nice name. How old are you?

translations.fa: {you}! چه اسم قشنگی. چند سالته؟

branches.suggestion: I'm thirty.
I'm a grown-up! How old are you?

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: I'm five. Five and a half! This is my teddy. His name's Mr Buttons.

translations.fa: من پنج سالمه. پنج و نیم! این عروسک خرسمه. اسمش آقای دکمه است.

branches.suggestion: Hello, Mr Buttons!
He's lovely. Is he your friend?

cultureNote.en: Brits say "lovely" all the time — about people, food, weather, anything nice.
cultureNote.fa: بریتانیایی‌ها مدام «lovely» می‌گویند — دربارهٔ آدم، غذا، هوا، هر چیز خوب.

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: Yes! He's my best friend. Are you from London?

translations.fa: آره! بهترین دوستمه. اهل لندنی؟

branches.suggestion: No, I'm from Iran.
No, I'm not. I'm from far away.
branches.suggestionFa: نه، نیستم. از راه دوری اومدم.

recasts.echo: Oh, you're from Iran? Wow!

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Wow! Is it hot there? Mummy says it's always cold here.

translations.fa: وای! اونجا گرمه؟ مامان می‌گه اینجا همیشه سرده.

branches.suggestion: Yes, it's very hot in summer.
Sometimes. It's cold in winter too.

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: Look, that's my mum. Her name's Leslie. She's a teacher.

translations.fa: ببین، اون مامانمه. اسمش لزلیه. معلمه.

branches.suggestion: Nice! Is she your teacher too?
branches.suggestionFa: چه خوب! معلم تو هم هست؟

branches.suggestion: Hello, Leslie!

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Hello, love! Welcome. Is Nicola talking your ear off?

translations.fa: سلام عزیزم! خوش اومدی. نیکولا داره سرت را می‌خوره؟

branches.suggestion: No, she's really sweet.
A little bit! But it's fine.

cultureNote.en: "Talk your ear off" means talk a lot. It's said with a smile.
cultureNote.fa: «talk your ear off» یعنی زیاد حرف زدن؛ با لبخند گفته می‌شود.

n8.speaker: nicola
n8.text: I'm not! I'm just friendly. Are you friendly too, {you}?

translations.fa: نه خیر! فقط مهربونم. تو هم مهربونی، {you}؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I am!
Of course I'm friendly!

n9.speaker: nicola
n9.text: Good! You're my friend now. Bye-bye, see you later!

translations.fa: خوبه! حالا تو دوست منی. بای‌بای، بعداً می‌بینمت!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Come and meet everyone, love. This is my husband, Tom.

translations.fa: بیا با همه آشنا شو عزیزم. این شوهرم، تامه.

branches.suggestion: Hello, Tom. Nice to meet you.
Hi Tom!

cultureNote.en: When you meet someone new, "Nice to meet you" is perfect. A handshake is normal with adults.
cultureNote.fa: وقتی با کسی آشنا می‌شوی، «Nice to meet you» عالی است. دست دادن با بزرگسالان عادی است.

n2.speaker: tom
n2.text: Alright? Good to have you here. Fancy a cuppa later?

translations.fa: چطوری؟ خوشحالم که اینجایی. بعداً یه چای می‌خوری؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, please. Thank you.
Maybe later, thanks.

recasts.echo: You'd love a cuppa? Brilliant.
recasts.better: Yes, please — I'd love a cuppa.
recasts.betterFa: بله لطفاً — یه چای عالی می‌شه.

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: And this little monkey is William. He's our youngest. He's three.

translations.fa: و این کوچولوی شیطون ویلیامه. کوچیک‌ترین بچه‌مونه. سه سالشه.

branches.suggestion: Hello, William! He's so cute.
Is he your son?

n4.speaker: william
n4.text: Hiya! I'm William! I'm three!

translations.fa: سلام! من ویلیامم! سه سالمه!

branches.suggestion: Hello, little one!
Three? Wow, you're big!

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: He loves saying hello! Ryan is upstairs. He's our son too. He's fifteen.

translations.fa: عاشق سلام کردنه! رایان طبقهٔ بالاست. اونم پسرمونه. پونزده سالشه.

branches.suggestion: So you have two sons and a daughter?
branches.suggestionFa: پس دو پسر و یه دختر دارید؟

branches.suggestion: Fifteen? He's a teenager!

cultureNote.en: In Britain, children are often called "the kids". Families usually have 2 or 3.
cultureNote.fa: در بریتانیا به بچه‌ها اغلب «the kids» می‌گویند.

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: That's right — three kids! And this is Margaret, Tom's mum. The kids call her Nana Maggie.

translations.fa: درسته — سه تا بچه! و این مارگارته، مامان تام. بچه‌ها صداش می‌کنن نانا مگی.

branches.suggestion: Hello, Margaret. Nice to meet you.
So she's the grandma?

n7.speaker: weda
n7.text: Hello, dear. Yes, I'm Nana to the children. Are you hungry?

translations.fa: سلام عزیزم. بله، من برای بچه‌ها «نانا» هستم. گرسنه‌ای؟

branches.suggestion: A little, yes.
No, I'm fine, thank you.

n8.speaker: leslie
n8.text: Right — that's the whole family. Questions? Who is Tom?

translations.fa: خب — این کل خانواده‌ست. سؤالی هست؟ تام کیه؟

branches.suggestion: Tom is your husband.
He's the dad!

n9.speaker: leslie
n9.text: Perfect! You've got a great memory. Welcome to the family, love.

translations.fa: عالی! حافظهٔ خوبی داری. به خانواده خوش اومدی عزیزم.

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Good morning, {you}! How are you today?

translations.fa: صبح بخیر، {you}! امروز حالت چطوره؟

branches.suggestion: I'm fine, thanks. And you?
I'm a bit tired today.

cultureNote.en: "How are you?" usually wants a short answer: "Fine, thanks. You?" — not a long story.
cultureNote.fa: «How are you?» معمولاً جواب کوتاه می‌خواهد.

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: I'm happy! It's pancake day! Are you happy?

translations.fa: من خوشحالم! امروز روز پنکیکه! تو خوشحالی؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I'm very happy!
Pancake day? What's that?

cultureNote.en: Pancake Day (Shrove Tuesday) is in February or March. Brits eat pancakes with lemon and sugar.
cultureNote.fa: روز پنکیک در فوریه یا مارس است. بریتانیایی‌ها پنکیک را با لیمو و شکر می‌خورند.

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: We eat pancakes with lemon and sugar. Yummy! Mr Buttons is sad, though.

translations.fa: پنکیک را با لیمو و شکر می‌خوریم. به‌به! ولی آقای دکمه ناراحته.

branches.suggestion: Oh no! Why is he sad?
Poor Mr Buttons!

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: He's hungry! Teddies are always hungry. Are you hungry?

translations.fa: گرسنه‌ست! خرس‌ها همیشه گرسنه‌اند. تو گرسنه‌ای؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I'm starving!
Not really.

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Me too! Ryan is grumpy in the morning. He's always grumpy.

translations.fa: منم! رایان صبح‌ها بداخلاقه. همیشه بداخلاقه.

branches.suggestion: Maybe he's just sleepy.
What does grumpy mean?

n6.speaker: ryan
n6.text: I'm not grumpy. I'm just knackered. Morning.

translations.fa: بداخلاق نیستم. فقط خیلی خسته‌ام. صبح بخیر.

branches.suggestion: Morning, Ryan. Are you OK?
Good morning! Knackered means tired, right?
branches.suggestionFa: صبح بخیر! knackered یعنی خسته، درسته؟

cultureNote.en: "Knackered" is very British slang for very tired. Friendly, but not for job interviews!
cultureNote.fa: «knackered» عامیانهٔ بریتانیایی یعنی خیلی خسته — نه برای مصاحبهٔ کاری!

n7.speaker: ryan
n7.text: Yeah, I'm OK. Just need a cup of tea. How are you finding it here?

translations.fa: آره خوبم. فقط یه چای لازم دارم. اینجا را چطور می‌بینی؟

branches.suggestion: It's great. Everyone is very kind.
It's new, but I'm excited.

n8.speaker: nicola
n8.text: Everyone is happy now! Even Ryan. Look, he's smiling!

translations.fa: حالا همه خوشحالن! حتی رایان. ببین، داره لبخند می‌زنه!

branches.suggestion: Ha! Yes, he is.
Smiling is good!

n9.speaker: nicola
n9.text: Yay! Let's have pancakes. See you at the table!

translations.fa: آخ جون! بیا پنکیک بخوریم. سر میز می‌بینمت!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: In this house we say please and thank you. Can you pass the milk, please?

translations.fa: توی این خونه لطفاً و ممنون می‌گیم. می‌شه شیر را بدی، لطفاً؟

branches.suggestion: Here you are.
Of course. Here's the milk.

cultureNote.en: When you give something, say "Here you are" or "There you go".
cultureNote.fa: وقتی چیزی می‌دهی بگو «Here you are» یا «There you go».

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: Thank you, love. Now you ask me. What do you want?

translations.fa: ممنون عزیزم. حالا تو از من بخواه. چی می‌خوای؟

branches.suggestion: Can I have the bread, please?
branches.suggestionFa: می‌شه نان را داشته باشم، لطفاً؟

branches.suggestion: Could you pass the butter, please?

recasts.echo: The bread? Here you are, love.
recasts.better: Can I have the bread, please?
recasts.betterFa: می‌شه نان را داشته باشم، لطفاً؟

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: Lovely manners! Oops — sorry, I knocked your cup.

translations.fa: چه ادب قشنگی! اوه — ببخشید، به فنجونت خوردم.

branches.suggestion: That's OK, no problem.
Don't worry about it.

cultureNote.en: Brits say sorry A LOT — even when it isn't their fault. "No worries" is a relaxed reply.
cultureNote.fa: بریتانیایی‌ها خیلی زیاد sorry می‌گویند — حتی وقتی تقصیر آن‌ها نیست.

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: Mummy, Mummy! Give me the jam!

translations.fa: مامان، مامان! مربا را بده!

branches.suggestion: Nicola, say please!
What's the magic word?

cultureNote.en: Parents ask children "What's the magic word?" — the answer is "please".
cultureNote.fa: والدین از بچه‌ها می‌پرسند «کلمهٔ جادویی چیه؟» — جواب «please» است.

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Pleeease can I have the jam? Thank you very much!

translations.fa: لطفاً می‌شه مربا را بدی؟ خیلی ممنون!

branches.suggestion: Good girl! You're welcome.
Very polite, Nicola!

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: Ha! Now, I need to get past you. What do I say?

translations.fa: ها! حالا باید از کنارت رد شم. چی بگم؟

branches.suggestion: Excuse me, can I get past?
Excuse me, please.

newWords.fa: ببخشید (برای رد شدن یا جلب توجه)

cultureNote.en: "Excuse me" is before (to pass, to ask). "Sorry" is after (a mistake).
cultureNote.fa: «Excuse me» قبل از کار است، «Sorry» بعد از اشتباه.

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Perfect. And if you don't hear someone?

translations.fa: عالی. و اگه حرف کسی را نشنیدی؟

branches.suggestion: Sorry?
Pardon?

cultureNote.en: Say "Sorry?" or "Pardon?" — never just "What?", which sounds rude.
cultureNote.fa: بگو «Sorry?» یا «Pardon?» — نه «What?» که بی‌ادبانه است.

n8.speaker: tom
n8.text: Blimey, it's like a manners school in here! Cheers for the tea, love.

translations.fa: ای بابا، اینجا مثل مدرسهٔ ادبه! مرسی بابت چای عزیزم.

branches.suggestion: Cheers means thank you, right?
Ha! Thank you, Tom.

n9.speaker: leslie
n9.text: Exactly. Cheers, ta, thanks — all mean thank you. You're a quick learner!

translations.fa: دقیقاً. cheers، ta، thanks — همه یعنی ممنون. تو سریع یاد می‌گیری!

n1.speaker: tom
n1.text: Morning! Kettle's on. Would you like a cup of tea?

translations.fa: صبح بخیر! کتری روشنه. یه فنجون چای میل داری؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, please. I'd love one.
No, thank you. Have you got coffee?

recasts.echo: Ah, you'd love a cuppa? Coming up!
recasts.better: Yes, please — I'd love a cup of tea.
recasts.betterFa: بله لطفاً — یه فنجون چای عالی می‌شه.

n2.speaker: tom
n2.text: We've got both. Milk? Most people here have milk in their tea.

translations.fa: هر دو داریم. شیر؟ بیشتر مردم اینجا چای را با شیر می‌خورن.

branches.suggestion: Yes, a little milk, please.
No milk for me, thanks.

cultureNote.en: Most Brits drink tea with milk. Black tea without milk is less common.
cultureNote.fa: بیشتر بریتانیایی‌ها چای را با شیر می‌نوشند.

n3.speaker: tom
n3.text: And sugar? One or two?

translations.fa: و شکر؟ یکی یا دوتا؟

branches.suggestion: One sugar, please.
No sugar, thanks. I'm sweet enough!
branches.suggestionFa: شکر نه، ممنون. خودم به اندازهٔ کافی شیرینم!

cultureNote.en: "I'm sweet enough" is a classic little joke when you refuse sugar.
cultureNote.fa: «I'm sweet enough» شوخی معروفی است وقتی شکر نمی‌خواهی.

n4.speaker: tom
n4.text: Ha! Here you go. Careful, it's hot. Would you like a biscuit too?

translations.fa: ها! بفرما. مواظب باش، داغه. بیسکویت هم میل داری؟

branches.suggestion: Ooh, yes please. What kind?
No, thank you. Just tea.

cultureNote.en: British vs American: biscuit (UK) = cookie (US). A "cookie" in the UK is a big soft one.
cultureNote.fa: biscuit (بریتانیا) = cookie (آمریکا).

n5.speaker: tom
n5.text: Chocolate digestives. The best! Leslie, do you want a tea, love?

translations.fa: دایجستیو شکلاتی. بهترینه! لزلی، چای می‌خوای عزیزم؟

branches.suggestion: I can make it!
She's busy, I think.

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: Oh, yes please, love! Strong, with milk, no sugar.

translations.fa: اوه، بله لطفاً عزیزم! پررنگ، با شیر، بدون شکر.

branches.suggestion: Strong with milk. Got it!
Is this one OK?

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Mmm, perfect. Thank you! You make a lovely cup of tea.

translations.fa: ممم، عالیه. ممنون! چای خوبی درست می‌کنی.

branches.suggestion: You're welcome!
Thanks, Tom showed me.

n8.speaker: tom
n8.text: Our guest makes the tea now. Best news all week! Cheers!

translations.fa: حالا مهمونمون چای درست می‌کنه. بهترین خبر این هفته! به سلامتی!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Right, breakfast! We've got toast, cereal and eggs. What would you like?

translations.fa: خب، صبحانه! نان تست، غلات و تخم‌مرغ داریم. چی میل داری؟

branches.suggestion: I'd like some toast, please.
Can I have an egg, please?
branches.suggestionFa: می‌شه یه تخم‌مرغ داشته باشم، لطفاً؟

cultureNote.en: Say "an egg" (vowel sound) but "a piece of toast".
cultureNote.fa: بگو «an egg» (صدای مصوت) ولی «a piece of toast».

recasts.echo: Toast? Lovely choice — coming right up.

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: Good choice. Butter and jam, or Marmite?

translations.fa: انتخاب خوبیه. کره و مربا، یا مارمایت؟

branches.suggestion: Butter and jam, please.
What's Marmite?

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: Marmite is yucky! It's black and salty.

translations.fa: مارمایت بدمزه‌ست! سیاه و شوره.

branches.suggestion: Yucky? Let me try it!
OK, no Marmite for me then.
branches.suggestionFa: باشه، پس برای من مارمایت نه.

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: Nicola, some people love it! Would you like orange juice?

translations.fa: نیکولا، بعضیا عاشقشن! آب پرتقال میل داری؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, a glass of orange juice, please.
branches.suggestionFa: بله، یه لیوان آب پرتقال، لطفاً.

branches.suggestion: Just water for me, thanks.

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: Here's a plate and a knife. Can you pass Nicola a spoon?

translations.fa: اینم بشقاب و چاقو. می‌شه یه قاشق به نیکولا بدی؟

branches.suggestion: Here's a spoon, Nicola.
Which one is the spoon?

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: Thank you! I like cereal with lots of milk. Do you like cereal?

translations.fa: مرسی! غلات را با کلی شیر دوست دارم. تو غلات دوست داری؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I like it.
Not really. I prefer eggs.
branches.suggestionFa: نه زیاد. تخم‌مرغ را ترجیح می‌دم.

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Some more toast? There's plenty.

translations.fa: باز هم نان تست؟ زیاد هست.

branches.suggestion: No more for me, I'm full.
Yes, one more slice, please.

cultureNote.en: "I'm full" is polite and normal. You don't need to finish everything on your plate.
cultureNote.fa: گفتن «I'm full» مؤدبانه و عادی است.

n8.speaker: leslie
n8.text: Well done! That's a proper British breakfast. Off to school, Nicola!

translations.fa: آفرین! این یه صبحانهٔ واقعی بریتانیایی بود. نیکولا، برو مدرسه!

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Welcome to my tea party! Sit there, next to Mr Buttons.

translations.fa: به مهمونی چای من خوش اومدی! اونجا بشین، کنار آقای دکمه.

branches.suggestion: Thank you for inviting me!
Hello again, Mr Buttons!

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: Do you want a cake? We've got pink cake and chocolate cake.

translations.fa: کیک می‌خوای؟ کیک صورتی و کیک شکلاتی داریم.

branches.suggestion: Pink cake, please!
Chocolate, please. I love chocolate.

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: Here you are. It's pretend cake. Mmm, yummy! Is it nice?

translations.fa: بفرما. کیک خیالیه. ممم، به‌به! خوبه؟

branches.suggestion: It's delicious!
Mmm, it's really sweet.

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: Mr Buttons wants a sandwich. Can you make one?

translations.fa: آقای دکمه ساندویچ می‌خواد. می‌تونی یکی درست کنی؟

branches.suggestion: Of course. Cheese or ham?
Here's a jam sandwich for him.

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Cheese! He loves cheese. Now we need tea. Can you pour it?

translations.fa: پنیر! عاشق پنیره. حالا چای لازم داریم. می‌تونی بریزی؟

branches.suggestion: Pour, pour… there you go!
Is the teapot hot?

n6.speaker: william
n6.text: Me! Me! I want cake!

translations.fa: من! من! کیک می‌خوام!

branches.suggestion: Here you are, William!
Say please, William!

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: William, it's not real! Silly billy. Do you want an apple? A real one?

translations.fa: ویلیام، واقعی نیست! خنگول. سیب می‌خوای؟ یه واقعی؟

branches.suggestion: An apple is a good idea.
He's hungry, I think.

n8.speaker: leslie
n8.text: Here's a banana for William. What a lovely tea party!

translations.fa: این یه موز برای ویلیام. چه مهمونی چای قشنگی!

branches.suggestion: Thank you for the lovely party, Nicola.
It's the best tea party ever!

n9.speaker: nicola
n9.text: Come again tomorrow! Mr Buttons says bye-bye!

translations.fa: فردا دوباره بیا! آقای دکمه می‌گه بای‌بای!

n1.speaker: weda
n1.text: Let's make scones, dear. Can you get the flour? It's in the cupboard.

translations.fa: بیا اسکون درست کنیم عزیزم. آرد را میاری؟ توی کابینته.

branches.suggestion: Here's the flour.
Which cupboard is it in?

cultureNote.en: Scones are small British cakes, eaten with jam and cream at tea time.
cultureNote.fa: اسکون کیک کوچک بریتانیایی است که با مربا و خامه خورده می‌شود.

n2.speaker: weda
n2.text: The one by the fridge. Now we need butter, sugar and milk.

translations.fa: همونی که کنار یخچاله. حالا کره، شکر و شیر لازم داریم.

branches.suggestion: The milk is in the fridge.
I've got the butter and sugar.

n3.speaker: weda
n3.text: Lovely. Now, a bowl and a big spoon, please.

translations.fa: عالی. حالا یه کاسه و یه قاشق بزرگ، لطفاً.

branches.suggestion: Here's a big bowl.
Is this spoon big enough?
branches.suggestionFa: این قاشق به اندازهٔ کافی بزرگه؟

n4.speaker: weda
n4.text: Perfect. Mix it, mix it. Not too fast! Is it sticky?

translations.fa: عالی. همش بزن، همش بزن. نه خیلی تند! چسبناکه؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, it's very sticky!
No, it's quite dry.

n5.speaker: weda
n5.text: Add a little more milk. Good! Now we cut circles.

translations.fa: یه کم دیگه شیر اضافه کن. خوبه! حالا دایره می‌بُریم.

branches.suggestion: How many circles?
Can I cut them?

n6.speaker: weda
n6.text: Eight, I think. Into the oven for fifteen minutes. Careful, it's very hot.

translations.fa: فکر کنم هشت‌تا. پونزده دقیقه توی فر. مواظب باش، خیلی داغه.

branches.suggestion: I'll be careful.
Fifteen minutes. Shall I set a timer?

n7.speaker: weda
n7.text: Mmm, can you smell them? They're ready! Golden and warm.

translations.fa: ممم، بوشون را حس می‌کنی؟ آماده‌اند! طلایی و گرم.

branches.suggestion: They smell amazing!
Can we eat them now?

n8.speaker: weda
n8.text: Jam first, then cream. That's the Cornish way. Try one, dear.

translations.fa: اول مربا، بعد خامه. این روش کورنوالیه. یکی امتحان کن عزیزم.

branches.suggestion: Delicious! Thank you, Maggie.
You're a brilliant cook!

n9.speaker: weda
n9.text: You're a natural, dear. Next time, you can teach Nicola!

translations.fa: تو ذاتاً بلدی عزیزم. دفعهٔ بعد می‌تونی به نیکولا یاد بدی!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Come in! This is the hall. Shoes off here, please.

translations.fa: بیا تو! اینجا راهروئه. لطفاً کفش‌ها را اینجا دربیار.

branches.suggestion: OK, shoes off.
Where do I put my shoes?

cultureNote.en: Many British families take shoes off at home, but not all. Just ask: "Shoes off?"
cultureNote.fa: خیلی از خانواده‌ها در خانه کفش درمی‌آورند، ولی نه همه. فقط بپرس.

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: On the rack, next to the umbrellas. There are three floors in our house.

translations.fa: روی جاکفشی، کنار چترها. خونهٔ ما سه طبقه داره.

branches.suggestion: Three floors? It's a big house!
What's on each floor?

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: Downstairs there's a kitchen and a living room. There's a small garden too.

translations.fa: طبقهٔ پایین آشپزخونه و نشیمن هست. یه باغچهٔ کوچیک هم هست.

branches.suggestion: Is there a bathroom downstairs?
I love the garden!

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: There's a toilet downstairs. The bathroom is upstairs, with the bedrooms.

translations.fa: پایین یه دستشویی هست. حموم بالاست، با اتاق‌خواب‌ها.

branches.suggestion: How many bedrooms are there?
And where's my room?

cultureNote.en: Brits often say "the loo" for the toilet. "Where's the loo?" is fine.
cultureNote.fa: بریتانیایی‌ها اغلب به دستشویی «the loo» می‌گویند.

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: There are four bedrooms. Your room is in the loft, at the top.

translations.fa: چهار اتاق‌خواب هست. اتاق تو زیرشیروونیه، بالای بالا.

branches.suggestion: The loft sounds cosy.
What's a loft?

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: It's the room under the roof. It's got a lovely window. Let's go up!

translations.fa: اتاق زیر سقف شیروونیه. یه پنجرهٔ قشنگ داره. بریم بالا!

branches.suggestion: Wow, there's a great view!
It's small but lovely.

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: There's a bed, a desk and a wardrobe. Is there anything you need?

translations.fa: یه تخت، یه میز تحریر و یه کمد لباس هست. چیزی لازم داری؟

branches.suggestion: Could I have another blanket?
branches.suggestionFa: می‌شه یه پتوی دیگه داشته باشم؟

branches.suggestion: No, it's perfect. Thank you!

n8.speaker: leslie
n8.text: Of course, love. Make yourself at home!

translations.fa: حتماً عزیزم. راحت باش، خونهٔ خودته!

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Oh no! Where's Mr Buttons? I can't find him!

translations.fa: وای نه! آقای دکمه کجاست؟ نمی‌تونم پیداش کنم!

branches.suggestion: Don't worry, we can find him.
Is he in your bedroom?

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: No! I looked. Is he under the sofa? Can you look?

translations.fa: نه! نگاه کردم. زیر مبله؟ می‌تونی نگاه کنی؟

branches.suggestion: No, he isn't under the sofa.
I can see a sock under the sofa!

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: Yuck, Ryan's sock! Is Mr Buttons behind the curtains?

translations.fa: ایش، جوراب رایان! آقای دکمه پشت پرده‌هاست؟

branches.suggestion: Let me check behind the curtains.
branches.suggestionFa: بذار پشت پرده‌ها را نگاه کنم.

branches.suggestion: Not there, sorry.

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: What about on the shelf? Next to the books?

translations.fa: روی قفسه چی؟ کنار کتاب‌ها؟

branches.suggestion: There's a teapot on the shelf.
No, only books are there.

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: William! Have you got Mr Buttons?

translations.fa: ویلیام! آقای دکمه دست توئه؟

branches.suggestion: Look — William is smiling.
Maybe he's in the toy box.

cultureNote.en: British vs American: a jumper = a sweater; trousers = pants. In the UK, pants are underwear!
cultureNote.fa: jumper = sweater ؛ trousers = pants. در بریتانیا pants یعنی لباس زیر!

n6.speaker: william
n6.text: Teddy's in the box!

translations.fa: تدی تو جعبه‌ست!

branches.suggestion: In the toy box! Well done, William!
He's in the box, Nicola!

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: Mr Buttons! You're under the blocks! Thank you, thank you!

translations.fa: آقای دکمه! زیر بلوک‌هایی! مرسی، مرسی!

branches.suggestion: You're welcome. He's safe now.
Put him on your bed tonight.

n8.speaker: nicola
n8.text: Can you play hide and seek with me? You hide, I count!

translations.fa: با من قایم‌موشک بازی می‌کنی؟ تو قایم شو، من می‌شمرم!

branches.suggestion: OK! I'll hide behind the door.
Count to ten, then!

n9.speaker: nicola
n9.text: One, two, three… ready or not, here I come!

translations.fa: یک، دو، سه… آماده باشی یا نه، دارم میام!

n1.speaker: ryan
n1.text: Alright? Sorry, my room's a bit messy. Come in.

translations.fa: چطوری؟ ببخشید، اتاقم یه کم شلوغه. بیا تو.

branches.suggestion: It's not that bad!
Wow, it's really messy!

n2.speaker: ryan
n2.text: This is my desk. That's my laptop. And these are my football boots.

translations.fa: این میزمه. اون لپ‌تاپمه. و این‌ها کفش‌های فوتبالمه.

branches.suggestion: Do you play football?
Those boots are very muddy!

n3.speaker: ryan
n3.text: Every Saturday. Those posters on the wall are my team. Liverpool!

translations.fa: هر شنبه. اون پوسترهای روی دیوار تیممه. لیورپول!

branches.suggestion: Cool posters!
Is that your favourite player?

n4.speaker: ryan
n4.text: Yeah, that's Salah. Mum says I need to tidy up. Can you help?

translations.fa: آره، اون صلاحه. مامان می‌گه باید مرتب کنم. کمک می‌کنی؟

branches.suggestion: Sure. Where do these clothes go?
OK, but only for ten minutes!

n5.speaker: ryan
n5.text: Those T-shirts go in the drawer. These jeans go in the wardrobe.

translations.fa: اون تی‌شرت‌ها می‌رن توی کشو. این شلوار جین‌ها توی کمد.

branches.suggestion: Done! What about these books?
Is this drawer the right one?

n6.speaker: ryan
n6.text: Books go on the shelf. And this mug is from last week. Gross!

translations.fa: کتاب‌ها روی قفسه. این ماگ هم مال هفتهٔ پیشه. چندش!

branches.suggestion: Take it to the kitchen!
That's disgusting, Ryan!

n7.speaker: ryan
n7.text: Ha, fair enough. Look — the floor! I can see the floor!

translations.fa: ها، حق داری. ببین — کف اتاق! کف را می‌بینم!

branches.suggestion: Your mum will be so happy.
It looks great now.

n8.speaker: ryan
n8.text: Cheers, mate. You're a legend. Wanna play FIFA now?

translations.fa: مرسی رفیق. تو بی‌نظیری. حالا فیفا بازی کنیم؟

n1.speaker: weda
n1.text: Let's sit outside, dear. It's sunny today! Look at the flowers.

translations.fa: بیا بیرون بشینیم عزیزم. امروز آفتابیه! به گل‌ها نگاه کن.

branches.suggestion: The flowers are beautiful.
It's lovely and warm.

n2.speaker: weda
n2.text: There are red roses and yellow daffodils. What's your favourite colour?

translations.fa: رزهای قرمز و نرگس‌های زرد هست. رنگ محبوبت چیه؟

branches.suggestion: My favourite colour is blue.
I like red, like the roses.
branches.suggestionFa: من قرمز را دوست دارم، مثل رزها.

cultureNote.en: British spelling is "colour" and "favourite" — American is "color", "favorite".
cultureNote.fa: املای بریتانیایی «colour» و «favourite» است.

n3.speaker: weda
n3.text: There's a bird in the tree. Can you see it? It's a robin.

translations.fa: یه پرنده روی درخته. می‌بینیش؟ سینه‌سرخه.

branches.suggestion: Yes! It's got a red chest.
Where? I can't see it.

n4.speaker: weda
n4.text: There, on the fence. And there's a cat under the bench!

translations.fa: اونجا، روی نرده. و یه گربه زیر نیمکته!

branches.suggestion: Is that your cat?
Oh no, the cat can see the bird!
branches.suggestionFa: ای وای، گربه پرنده را می‌بینه!

n5.speaker: weda
n5.text: That's Mrs Patel's cat, Biscuit. Don't worry, she's too lazy!

translations.fa: اون گربهٔ خانم پاتله، بیسکویت. نگران نباش، خیلی تنبله!

branches.suggestion: Biscuit is a funny name!
She looks very fat and happy.
branches.suggestionFa: خیلی چاق و خوشحال به نظر میاد.

n6.speaker: weda
n6.text: The grass is long. Tom needs to cut it. There's a lot of work in a garden.

translations.fa: چمن‌ها بلندن. تام باید کوتاهشون کنه. باغچه کار زیادی داره.

branches.suggestion: I can help with the garden.
Do you like gardening?

cultureNote.en: Brits love their gardens. Even a tiny garden often has flowers, a shed and a bird feeder.
cultureNote.fa: بریتانیایی‌ها عاشق باغچه‌اند.

n7.speaker: weda
n7.text: I love it. Green fingers, my mum called it. Shall we water the plants?

translations.fa: عاشقشم. مادرم بهش می‌گفت «انگشت‌های سبز». به گیاه‌ها آب بدیم؟

branches.suggestion: Yes! Where's the watering can?
Green fingers? That's lovely.

n8.speaker: weda
n8.text: There we are. The garden looks happy now, and so do you, dear.

translations.fa: ایناهاش. حالا باغچه خوشحال به نظر میاد، تو هم همین‌طور عزیزم.

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Let's count the eggs! One, two, three… how many are there?

translations.fa: بیا تخم‌مرغ‌ها را بشمریم! یک، دو، سه… چندتاست؟

branches.suggestion: There are six eggs.
I think there are twelve.

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: Yes! Six eggs. Now the spoons. Seven, eight, nine, ten!

translations.fa: آره! شش‌تا تخم‌مرغ. حالا قاشق‌ها. هفت، هشت، نه، ده!

branches.suggestion: Ten spoons. Well done!
Can you count to twenty?

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen… what comes next?

translations.fa: یازده، دوازده، سیزده، چهارده، پانزده… بعدش چیه؟

branches.suggestion: Sixteen, seventeen, eighteen!
Next is sixteen.

cultureNote.en: Careful: thirTEEN (stress at the end) vs THIRty (stress at the start). Listen for it!
cultureNote.fa: دقت کن: thirteen (تأکید آخر) و thirty (تأکید اول).

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: Nineteen, twenty! I did it! How many biscuits are in the tin?

translations.fa: نوزده، بیست! تونستم! چندتا بیسکویت توی قوطیه؟

branches.suggestion: There are only two biscuits.
None! The tin is empty!

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Ryan ate them! Ryan always eats the biscuits. Can we bake some more?

translations.fa: رایان خوردشون! رایان همیشه بیسکویت‌ها را می‌خوره. می‌شه بیشتر بپزیم؟

branches.suggestion: Let's ask your mum first.
Good idea! How many shall we make?

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: Twenty! No, a hundred! A million biscuits!

translations.fa: بیست‌تا! نه، صدتا! یه میلیون بیسکویت!

branches.suggestion: A million is too many!
Maybe twelve is enough.

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: OK, twelve. One for me, one for you, one for Mr Buttons…

translations.fa: باشه، دوازده‌تا. یکی برای من، یکی برای تو، یکی برای آقای دکمه…

n1.speaker: ryan
n1.text: So how old are you? I'm sixteen. Seventeen in March!

translations.fa: خب چند سالته؟ من شونزده سالمه. مارس هفده می‌شم!

branches.suggestion: I'm twenty-five years old.
I'm older than you!

n2.speaker: ryan
n2.text: Nicola is six, William is one. Mum says she's "thirty-nine forever"!

translations.fa: نیکولا شش سالشه، ویلیام دو. مامان می‌گه «تا ابد سی‌ونه»!

branches.suggestion: Ha! Thirty-nine forever.
How old is your dad?

cultureNote.en: In Britain, asking an adult's age can be a bit rude. With friends it's fine, with strangers, avoid it.
cultureNote.fa: در بریتانیا پرسیدن سن بزرگسالان کمی بی‌ادبی است.

n3.speaker: ryan
n3.text: Dad's forty-two. Don't tell him I told you! Have you got a mobile?

translations.fa: بابا چهل‌ودوئه. بهش نگی من گفتم! موبایل داری؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I've got a mobile.
Yes, but it's very old.

cultureNote.en: British vs American: mobile (UK) = cell phone (US).
cultureNote.fa: mobile (بریتانیا) = cell phone (آمریکا).

n4.speaker: ryan
n4.text: What's your number? I'll add you to the family group chat.

translations.fa: شماره‌ات چنده؟ اضافه‌ات می‌کنم به گروه خانوادگی.

branches.suggestion: It's oh-seven-seven, double-four…
Can I write it down for you?

cultureNote.en: Brits say "oh" for zero in phone numbers, and "double four" for 44.
cultureNote.fa: بریتانیایی‌ها در شماره تلفن به صفر «oh» می‌گویند و ۴۴ را «double four».

n5.speaker: ryan
n5.text: Sorted. Warning — Nana sends forty messages a day. All emojis.

translations.fa: ردیف شد. هشدار — نانا روزی چهل‌تا پیام می‌فرسته. همه ایموجی.

branches.suggestion: That's so sweet!
Forty messages? Oh no!

n6.speaker: ryan
n6.text: You get used to it. Right, what's the Wi-Fi password again? Mum changed it.

translations.fa: عادت می‌کنی. خب، رمز وای‌فای چی بود؟ مامان عوضش کرد.

branches.suggestion: I don't know. Ask your mum!
Is it on the fridge?

n7.speaker: ryan
n7.text: Ha, it's on the fridge. "Tidy your room, Ryan, 2026." Classic Mum.

translations.fa: ها، روی یخچاله. «اتاقت را مرتب کن رایان ۲۰۲۶». مامانه دیگه.

n1.speaker: tom
n1.text: Morning! What time is it? I can't find my watch.

translations.fa: صبح بخیر! ساعت چنده؟ ساعتم را پیدا نمی‌کنم.

branches.suggestion: It's seven o'clock.
It's half past seven.

n2.speaker: tom
n2.text: Half past? I'm late! My train is at quarter to eight.

translations.fa: هفت و نیم؟ دیرم شده! قطارم یک‌ربع به هشته.

branches.suggestion: Hurry up! You've got fifteen minutes.
branches.suggestionFa: عجله کن! پونزده دقیقه وقت داری.

branches.suggestion: Don't worry, the station is close.

cultureNote.en: British trains are often late, so Brits always check the app! People say "Is it running on time?"
cultureNote.fa: قطارهای بریتانیا اغلب دیر می‌کنند.

n3.speaker: tom
n3.text: Where are my keys? Quick — are they on the table?

translations.fa: کلیدهام کجان؟ زود — روی میزن؟

branches.suggestion: Your keys are next to the kettle.
They're in your coat pocket.

n4.speaker: tom
n4.text: Got them, thanks! What time do you finish today?

translations.fa: پیداشون کردم، مرسی! امروز کِی تموم می‌کنی؟

branches.suggestion: I finish at five o'clock.
At quarter past four.

n5.speaker: tom
n5.text: Lovely. Tea is at six, then. Don't be late — Nana's making shepherd's pie!

translations.fa: عالیه. پس شام ساعت شیشه. دیر نکنی — نانا پای چوپان درست می‌کنه!

branches.suggestion: I won't be late. I promise!
Shepherd's pie? Yum!

cultureNote.en: In many British homes "tea" in the evening means dinner, the main meal!
cultureNote.fa: در بسیاری از خانه‌ها «tea» عصر یعنی شام!

n6.speaker: tom
n6.text: Right, I'm off. See you at six! Bye!

translations.fa: خب، من رفتم. ساعت شش می‌بینمت! خداحافظ!

branches.suggestion: Bye! Have a good day!
See you later, Tom!

n7.speaker: tom
n7.text: Oh — the time's on the oven clock! Silly me. Cheers!

translations.fa: آه — ساعت روی ساعت فره! چه گیجم. مرسی!

n1.speaker: doris
n1.text: Hello, duck. Is this the number twelve bus? My eyes aren't very good.

translations.fa: سلام عزیزم. این اتوبوس شماره دوازده‌ست؟ چشم‌هام خیلی خوب نمی‌بینه.

branches.suggestion: Yes, this is the number twelve.
No, this is the number twenty.

cultureNote.en: "Duck", "love", "pet" — friendly words strangers use in different parts of Britain.
cultureNote.fa: «duck»، «love»، «pet» — واژه‌های صمیمی در نقاط مختلف بریتانیا.

n2.speaker: doris
n2.text: Oh good. How much is a ticket to town? Two pounds?

translations.fa: آه خوبه. بلیت تا مرکز شهر چنده؟ دو پوند؟

branches.suggestion: It's two pounds fifty.
I think it's two pounds.

n3.speaker: doris
n3.text: Thank you, love. And when's the next stop? I get off at the library.

translations.fa: ممنون عزیزم. ایستگاه بعدی کِیه؟ من کنار کتابخونه پیاده می‌شم.

branches.suggestion: The library is in three stops.
I'm not sure. Let's ask the driver.
branches.suggestionFa: مطمئن نیستم. بیا از راننده بپرسیم.

n4.speaker: doris
n4.text: You're a kind one. Where are you going today?

translations.fa: تو آدم مهربونی هستی. امروز کجا می‌ری؟

branches.suggestion: I'm going to the supermarket.
I'm going to meet a friend.
branches.suggestionFa: دارم می‌رم یه دوست را ببینم.

n5.speaker: doris
n5.text: Lovely. In my day the bus was twenty pence! Twenty pence!

translations.fa: چه خوب. زمان ما اتوبوس بیست پنی بود! بیست پنی!

branches.suggestion: Twenty pence? That's very cheap!
Everything is expensive now.

cultureNote.en: 100 pence = 1 pound. People say "p": "fifty p".
cultureNote.fa: ۱۰۰ پنی = ۱ پوند. مردم می‌گویند «p».

n6.speaker: doris
n6.text: Here's my stop. Press the bell for me, would you? The red button.

translations.fa: ایستگاه منه. زنگ را برام می‌زنی؟ دکمهٔ قرمز.

branches.suggestion: Of course. There you go!
Done. Mind the step!

n7.speaker: doris
n7.text: Thank you, duck. Ta-ra! Thank you, driver!

translations.fa: ممنون عزیزم. خدانگهدار! ممنون آقای راننده!

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Wake up, sleepyhead! It's morning! What time do you get up?

translations.fa: بیدار شو، خوابالو! صبح شده! کِی از خواب پا می‌شی؟

branches.suggestion: I get up at seven.
I usually get up late.

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: I get up at six! I wake up Mummy and Daddy. They don't like it!

translations.fa: من ساعت شش پا می‌شم! مامان و بابا را بیدار می‌کنم. خوششون نمیاد!

branches.suggestion: Six o'clock is very early!
Poor Mummy and Daddy!

cultureNote.en: British children say "Mummy" and "Daddy"; older kids say "Mum" and "Dad". American is "Mom".
cultureNote.fa: کودکان بریتانیایی «Mummy» می‌گویند؛ بزرگ‌ترها «Mum». آمریکایی: «Mom».

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: Then I brush my teeth. Do you brush your teeth every morning?

translations.fa: بعد دندون‌هام را مسواک می‌زنم. تو هر صبح مسواک می‌زنی؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, every morning and every night.
branches.suggestionFa: آره، هر صبح و هر شب.

branches.suggestion: Of course I do!

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: Then I get dressed. I wear my school uniform. It's green!

translations.fa: بعد لباس می‌پوشم. یونیفرم مدرسه‌ام را می‌پوشم. سبزه!

branches.suggestion: I like your green jumper.
Do you like your uniform?

cultureNote.en: Almost all British schools have a uniform, often a jumper, a shirt and a tie.
cultureNote.fa: تقریباً همهٔ مدارس بریتانیا یونیفرم دارند.

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: It's itchy! Then I have breakfast. I have cereal. What do you have?

translations.fa: خارش‌داره! بعد صبحانه می‌خورم. سریال (غلات) می‌خورم. تو چی می‌خوری؟

branches.suggestion: I have toast and tea.
I don't have breakfast.

recasts.echo: You don't have breakfast?

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: You need breakfast! Nana says it's the most important meal.

translations.fa: تو صبحانه لازم داری! نانا می‌گه مهم‌ترین وعده‌ست.

branches.suggestion: Nana is right.
OK, I'll have some toast.
branches.suggestionFa: باشه، یه کم نون تست می‌خورم.

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: Then I go to school with Daddy. We walk. Bye bye!

translations.fa: بعد با بابا می‌رم مدرسه. پیاده می‌ریم. بای بای!

n1.speaker: ryan
n1.text: Ugh, Monday. I hate Mondays. What day do you like best?

translations.fa: اه، دوشنبه. از دوشنبه بدم میاد. کدوم روز را بیشتر دوست داری؟

branches.suggestion: I like Fridays best.
I like Saturday best. No work!
branches.suggestionFa: شنبه را بیشتر دوست دارم. کار نیست!

cultureNote.en: The British week starts on Monday. Saturday and Sunday are "the weekend".
cultureNote.fa: هفتهٔ بریتانیایی از دوشنبه شروع می‌شود.

n2.speaker: ryan
n2.text: Same. On Tuesdays I've got football. On Wednesdays Nicola goes to swimming.

translations.fa: منم. سه‌شنبه‌ها فوتبال دارم. چهارشنبه‌ها نیکولا می‌ره شنا.

branches.suggestion: Does she swim well?
And what does William do?

n3.speaker: ryan
n3.text: William goes to nursery. He plays with sand all day. Lucky him!

translations.fa: ویلیام می‌ره مهدکودک. کل روز با شن بازی می‌کنه. خوش به حالش!

branches.suggestion: He loves sand!
Nursery sounds fun.

n4.speaker: ryan
n4.text: Mum works at the hospital. She starts at eight and finishes at four.

translations.fa: مامان توی بیمارستان کار می‌کنه. ساعت هشت شروع می‌کنه و چهار تموم.

branches.suggestion: Is she a nurse?
That's a long day.

n5.speaker: ryan
n5.text: Yeah, she's a nurse. Dad works in an office. He drinks about ten cups of tea a day.

translations.fa: آره، پرستاره. بابا توی دفتر کار می‌کنه. روزی حدود ده لیوان چای می‌خوره.

branches.suggestion: Ten cups? That's a lot!
He really loves tea.

n6.speaker: ryan
n6.text: On Thursdays Nana comes for tea. On Sundays we have a roast. Best day!

translations.fa: پنجشنبه‌ها نانا برای شام میاد. یکشنبه‌ها کباب یکشنبه داریم. بهترین روز!

branches.suggestion: What's a roast?
I love Sunday dinner too!

cultureNote.en: Sunday roast: roast meat, potatoes, vegetables, Yorkshire puddings and gravy. A big British tradition.
cultureNote.fa: ناهار یکشنبه: گوشت کبابی، سیب‌زمینی، سبزیجات و سس. سنت بزرگ بریتانیایی.

n7.speaker: ryan
n7.text: Roast chicken, roast potatoes, gravy. Come this Sunday. Mum won't mind!

translations.fa: مرغ کبابی، سیب‌زمینی تنوری، سس. این یکشنبه بیا. مامان ناراحت نمی‌شه!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Bath time, William! Oh, can you help me? Pass me the towel, please.

translations.fa: وقت حمومه، ویلیام! آه، کمکم می‌کنی؟ لطفاً حوله را بده.

branches.suggestion: Here's the towel.
Which towel? The blue one?

n2.speaker: william
n2.text: Look! My duck's in the bath!

translations.fa: ببین! اردکم تو وانه!

branches.suggestion: Here's your rubber duck, William.
Quack quack!

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: He loves that duck. Do you have a bath or a shower in the morning?

translations.fa: عاشق اون اردکه. تو صبح‌ها وان می‌گیری یا دوش؟

branches.suggestion: I have a shower every morning.
I prefer a bath at night.

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: Does the water feel OK, William? Not too hot?

translations.fa: آب خوبه، ویلیام؟ خیلی داغ نیست؟

branches.suggestion: Let me check the water.
Is it OK, William?

n5.speaker: william
n5.text: Mummy, the water's cold!

translations.fa: مامان، آب سرده!

branches.suggestion: Let's add some hot water.
branches.suggestionFa: بیا یه کم آب گرم اضافه کنیم.

branches.suggestion: Turn on the hot tap.
branches.suggestionFa: شیر آب گرم را باز کن.

cultureNote.en: Old British bathrooms often have two taps: one hot, one cold!
cultureNote.fa: حمام‌های قدیمی بریتانیا اغلب دو شیر دارند: یکی گرم، یکی سرد!

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: That's better. Can you pass the shampoo? It's next to the soap.

translations.fa: بهتر شد. شامپو را می‌دی؟ کنار صابونه.

branches.suggestion: Here you are. Shampoo.
I can only see the soap.

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Eyes closed, William! Good boy. Does he do this every night? Yes, every night!

translations.fa: چشم‌ها بسته، ویلیام! آفرین پسر خوب. هر شب این کار را می‌کنه؟ آره، هر شب!

branches.suggestion: He's very good in the bath.
Every night? That's hard work!

n8.speaker: leslie
n8.text: All done. Now pyjamas, a story and bed. Night night, little one!

translations.fa: تموم شد. حالا پیژامه، قصه و تخت. شب بخیر کوچولو!

n1.speaker: weda
n1.text: I'm an early bird, dear. I always get up at half past five.

translations.fa: من سحرخیزم عزیزم. همیشه ساعت پنج و نیم پا می‌شم.

branches.suggestion: Half past five! Why so early?
branches.suggestionFa: پنج و نیم! چرا اینقدر زود؟

branches.suggestion: I never get up that early.
branches.suggestionFa: من هیچ‌وقت اینقدر زود پا نمی‌شم.

n2.speaker: weda
n2.text: I always have a cup of tea first. Then I usually read the newspaper.

translations.fa: همیشه اول یه فنجون چای می‌خورم. بعد معمولاً روزنامه می‌خونم.

branches.suggestion: Do you read the paper every day?
I usually read the news on my phone.
branches.suggestionFa: معمولاً اخبار را روی گوشیم می‌خونم.

n3.speaker: weda
n3.text: Every day. Then I sometimes go for a walk with Mrs Patel.

translations.fa: هر روز. بعد گاهی با خانم پاتل پیاده‌روی می‌رم.

branches.suggestion: Do you walk in the park?
Walking is good for you.

n4.speaker: weda
n4.text: Yes, round the park. Then on Mondays I always go to the market.

translations.fa: آره، دور پارک. بعد دوشنبه‌ها همیشه می‌رم بازار.

branches.suggestion: What do you buy at the market?
I love markets too.

n5.speaker: weda
n5.text: Fruit, vegetables, and a bit of gossip! Do you ever watch telly in the afternoon?

translations.fa: میوه، سبزی و یه کم غیبت! تو هیچ‌وقت عصرها تلویزیون می‌بینی؟

branches.suggestion: Sometimes I watch telly.
No, I'm usually at work.

cultureNote.en: British vs American: telly / TV (UK) = TV (US). A "programme" (UK) = a "show" (US).
cultureNote.fa: telly (بریتانیا) = TV؛ programme = show.

n6.speaker: weda
n6.text: I never miss my quiz programme at five. And I always go to bed at ten.

translations.fa: هیچ‌وقت مسابقهٔ ساعت پنجم را از دست نمی‌دم. و همیشه ساعت ده می‌خوابم.

branches.suggestion: Early to bed, early to rise!
What time do you have tea?

n7.speaker: weda
n7.text: Tea at six, always. Some things never change, dear.

translations.fa: شام ساعت شش، همیشه. بعضی چیزها هیچ‌وقت عوض نمی‌شن عزیزم.

n1.speaker: tom
n1.text: Have you seen outside? What's the weather like today?

translations.fa: بیرون را دیدی؟ امروز هوا چطوره؟

branches.suggestion: It's raining again.
It's grey and cloudy.

cultureNote.en: British spelling: grey. American: gray. Brits talk about the weather all the time — it's a great way to start a chat.
cultureNote.fa: املای بریتانیایی grey است. حرف زدن از هوا راه خوبی برای شروع گفت‌وگوست.

n2.speaker: tom
n2.text: Typical! It was sunny an hour ago. British weather, eh?

translations.fa: طبق معمول! یه ساعت پیش آفتابی بود. هوای بریتانیا دیگه!

branches.suggestion: Four seasons in one day!
Is it always like this?

n3.speaker: tom
n3.text: Pretty much! Take an umbrella. And put your coat on. It's windy too.

translations.fa: تقریباً! چتر بردار. و کتت را بپوش. باد هم میاد.

branches.suggestion: Good idea. Where's my umbrella?
I don't need a coat. I'm fine.

recasts.echo: You don't need a coat?

n4.speaker: tom
n4.text: Trust me, you do! It's only eight degrees. That's cold for October.

translations.fa: به من اعتماد کن، لازم داری! فقط هشت درجه‌ست. برای اکتبر سرده.

branches.suggestion: Eight degrees? Brr, that's cold!
In my country it's hot in October.

n5.speaker: tom
n5.text: Lucky you! Here, it's wet from October to March. Do you like the rain?

translations.fa: خوش به حالت! اینجا از اکتبر تا مارس خیسه. بارون دوست داری؟

branches.suggestion: I love the sound of rain.
No, I prefer the sun.

n6.speaker: tom
n6.text: Me too. Look — it's stopped! Oh, no it hasn't. It's chucking it down!

translations.fa: منم. ببین — بند اومد! آه، نه، نیومد. داره سیل‌آسا می‌باره!

branches.suggestion: What does "chucking it down" mean?
Wow, really heavy rain!

n7.speaker: tom
n7.text: It means very heavy rain. Stay dry! And wear your wellies!

translations.fa: یعنی بارون خیلی شدید. خشک بمونی! و چکمه‌های لاستیکیت را بپوش!

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Let's play dressing up! I've got a pink dress. What have you got?

translations.fa: بیا لباس‌بازی کنیم! من یه پیرهن صورتی دارم. تو چی داری؟

branches.suggestion: I've got a big blue hat.
branches.suggestionFa: من یه کلاه آبی بزرگ دارم.

branches.suggestion: I've got a yellow scarf.

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: Has Mr Buttons got a hat? No, he hasn't! Let's give him a hat.

translations.fa: آقای دکمه کلاه داره؟ نه، نداره! بیا بهش یه کلاه بدیم.

branches.suggestion: Here — a little red hat for him.
branches.suggestionFa: بیا — یه کلاه قرمز کوچولو براش.

branches.suggestion: He looks so funny in a hat!

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: Now shoes! Have you got wellies? Mine are purple with spots!

translations.fa: حالا کفش! چکمهٔ لاستیکی داری؟ مال من بنفشه با خال‌خال!

branches.suggestion: No, I've only got trainers.
Purple with spots? Lovely!

cultureNote.en: British vs American: trainers (UK) = sneakers (US). Wellies = rain boots.
cultureNote.fa: trainers (بریتانیا) = sneakers (آمریکا).

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: Daddy's got a big brown jumper. It's soooo big! Put it on!

translations.fa: بابا یه ژاکت قهوه‌ای بزرگ داره. خیلی بزرگه! بپوشش!

branches.suggestion: It's too big for me!
OK! Do I look silly?

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Yes! You look like a bear! Now trousers. The orange ones!

translations.fa: آره! شبیه خرس شدی! حالا شلوار. نارنجیه را!

branches.suggestion: Orange trousers? No way!
Fine, the orange ones.

cultureNote.en: Careful! In the UK, "pants" means underwear. Say "trousers" for what Americans call pants.
cultureNote.fa: دقت! در بریتانیا pants یعنی لباس زیر. بگو trousers.

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: Ha ha! Mummy, look! Take a photo! Smile!

translations.fa: ها ها! مامان، ببین! عکس بگیر! لبخند بزن!

branches.suggestion: Cheese!
Wait, let me fix my hat.
branches.suggestionFa: صبر کن، کلاهم را درست کنم.

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: That's the best photo ever. You're my best dressing-up friend!

translations.fa: این بهترین عکس دنیاست. تو بهترین دوست لباس‌بازی منی!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Right, everyone! Shoes on! Coats on! We leave in five minutes!

translations.fa: خب همه! کفش‌ها پا! کت‌ها تن! پنج دقیقه دیگه راه می‌افتیم!

branches.suggestion: I'm ready!
Five minutes? OK, hurry up, everyone!
branches.suggestionFa: پنج دقیقه؟ باشه، عجله کنید همه!

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: Can you help Nicola? Put her coat on, please. Zip it up — it's cold.

translations.fa: به نیکولا کمک می‌کنی؟ لطفاً کتش را تنش کن. زیپش را بکش — سرده.

branches.suggestion: Arms in, Nicola. There!
Nicola, stand still, please!

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: I can't find my other glove! Where is it?

translations.fa: دستکش دیگه‌ام را پیدا نمی‌کنم! کجاست؟

branches.suggestion: Look in your coat pocket.
branches.suggestionFa: توی جیب کتت را نگاه کن.

branches.suggestion: Here it is, on the stairs.

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: Brilliant. Ryan! Don't forget your PE kit! And don't forget your lunch!

translations.fa: عالیه. رایان! وسایل ورزشت یادت نره! ناهارت هم یادت نره!

branches.suggestion: Ryan! Your mum's calling you!
I'll get Ryan's bag.

n5.speaker: ryan
n5.text: Yeah, yeah. Don't panic, Mum.

translations.fa: آره، آره. هول نکن مامان.

branches.suggestion: Ryan, here's your lunch box.
Your PE bag is by the door.

cultureNote.en: PE = Physical Education, sport at school. A "packed lunch" is food from home.
cultureNote.fa: PE یعنی تربیت‌بدنی. packed lunch یعنی غذای خانگی.

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: William, don't eat that! Put it down! What has he got?

translations.fa: ویلیام، اونو نخور! بذارش زمین! چی دستشه؟

branches.suggestion: It's a crayon! Give it to me, William.
branches.suggestionFa: مداد شمعیه! بدش به من ویلیام.

branches.suggestion: Don't worry, it's only a biscuit.

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Phew. OK — bags? Check. Keys? Check. Let's go! Close the door behind you!

translations.fa: آخیش. خب — کیف‌ها؟ هست. کلیدها؟ هست. بریم! در را پشت سرت ببند!

branches.suggestion: Door closed. Let's go!
Wait! Is the back door locked?

n8.speaker: leslie
n8.text: Good thinking. Every morning is like this! Thanks for your help, love.

translations.fa: فکر خوبیه. هر صبح همینطوره! ممنون از کمکت عزیزم.

n1.speaker: weda
n1.text: Come and sit with me, dear. I'm knitting a scarf for William.

translations.fa: بیا پیش من بشین عزیزم. دارم برای ویلیام شال‌گردن می‌بافم.

branches.suggestion: It's lovely! What colour is it?
I can't knit. Is it difficult?

n2.speaker: weda
n2.text: It's red and white stripes. Which colour do you like, the red or the white?

translations.fa: راه‌راه قرمز و سفیده. کدوم رنگ را دوست داری، قرمز یا سفید؟

branches.suggestion: I like the red one.
The white one, I think.

n3.speaker: weda
n3.text: Good choice. Next I'll make a hat and some mittens. It gets very cold in winter.

translations.fa: انتخاب خوبیه. بعد یه کلاه و دستکش بی‌انگشت می‌بافم. زمستون خیلی سرد می‌شه.

branches.suggestion: Does it snow here?
What are mittens?

n4.speaker: weda
n4.text: Sometimes it snows, but not much. Mostly it's just cold, wet and dark.

translations.fa: گاهی برف میاد، ولی نه زیاد. بیشتر فقط سرد، خیس و تاریکه.

branches.suggestion: When does it get dark?
That sounds a bit sad.
branches.suggestionFa: یه کم غم‌انگیز به نظر میاد.

n5.speaker: weda
n5.text: Around four o'clock in December! But we have cosy jumpers and hot chocolate.

translations.fa: حدود ساعت چهار تو دسامبر! ولی ژاکت‌های گرم و شکلات داغ داریم.

branches.suggestion: I love hot chocolate!
Four o'clock? That's early!

cultureNote.en: In winter British people say "Wrap up warm!" — wear lots of warm clothes.
cultureNote.fa: در زمستان بریتانیایی‌ها می‌گویند «Wrap up warm!».

n6.speaker: weda
n6.text: Here, hold the wool for me. Hold it up, like this. That's it!

translations.fa: بیا، کاموا را برام نگه دار. بالا نگهش دار، اینجوری. همینه!

branches.suggestion: Like this?
Oops, I dropped it!

n7.speaker: weda
n7.text: Perfect. One day I'll teach you. Wrap up warm when you go out, dear!

translations.fa: عالیه. یه روز بهت یاد می‌دم. وقتی بیرون می‌ری خودت را گرم بپوشون عزیزم!

n1.speaker: baker
n1.text: Morning! What can I get you, love?

translations.fa: صبح بخیر! چی میل دارید عزیزم؟

branches.suggestion: Can I have a loaf of bread, please?
branches.suggestionFa: می‌شه یه قرص نون بدید لطفاً؟

branches.suggestion: Morning! Just looking, thanks.
branches.suggestionFa: صبح بخیر! فقط دارم نگاه می‌کنم، ممنون.

n2.speaker: baker
n2.text: White or brown? This one's fresh from the oven.

translations.fa: سفید یا سبوس‌دار؟ این یکی تازه از فر دراومده.

branches.suggestion: This one, please. The brown one.
That white one looks nice.
branches.suggestionFa: اون سفیده خوب به نظر میاد.

n3.speaker: baker
n3.text: Lovely choice. Anything else? The sausage rolls are still warm.

translations.fa: انتخاب خوبیه. چیز دیگه؟ رول سوسیس‌ها هنوز گرمن.

branches.suggestion: How much are the sausage rolls?
What's that, next to the cakes?

n4.speaker: baker
n4.text: Sausage rolls are one pound twenty. Those are Eccles cakes — currants inside.

translations.fa: رول سوسیس یک پوند و بیسته. اونا کیک اکلزن — توشون کشمش داره.

branches.suggestion: Two sausage rolls, please.
I'll try an Eccles cake.

cultureNote.en: Bakeries like Greggs sell sausage rolls — a very popular British snack.
cultureNote.fa: نانوایی‌هایی مثل گرگز رول سوسیس می‌فروشند — یک خوراکی محبوب بریتانیایی.

n5.speaker: baker
n5.text: Good stuff. Would you like a bag? It's ten p for a bag.

translations.fa: عالیه. کیسه می‌خواید؟ کیسه ده پنیه.

branches.suggestion: No thanks, I've got my own bag.
branches.suggestionFa: نه ممنون، کیسهٔ خودم را دارم.

branches.suggestion: Yes, please. One bag.

cultureNote.en: UK shops charge for plastic bags, so people bring their own "bag for life".
cultureNote.fa: فروشگاه‌های بریتانیا برای کیسه پول می‌گیرند.

n6.speaker: baker
n6.text: That's four pounds thirty altogether. Card or cash?

translations.fa: روی هم چهار پوند و سی میشه. کارت یا نقد؟

branches.suggestion: Card, please. Can I tap?
Cash. Here's a five-pound note.
branches.suggestionFa: نقد. بفرمایید یه اسکناس پنج پوندی.

n7.speaker: baker
n7.text: Lovely, thanks. Seventy p change. Have a nice day! See you tomorrow!

translations.fa: عالیه، ممنون. هفتاد پنی باقی‌مونده. روز خوش! فردا می‌بینمتون!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Right, here's the list. Milk, eggs, apples and washing-up liquid. Can you help me find things?

translations.fa: خب، این فهرسته. شیر، تخم‌مرغ، سیب و مایع ظرفشویی. کمکم می‌کنی پیداشون کنم؟

branches.suggestion: Sure. Where's the milk?
I'll get the apples.

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: Milk is in aisle three, at the back. Get two pints, please.

translations.fa: شیر راهروی سه‌ست، ته فروشگاه. لطفاً دو پاینت بیار.

branches.suggestion: Two pints of milk. Got it!
What's a pint?

cultureNote.en: Milk is sold in pints in the UK, but most other things are in kilos and litres.
cultureNote.fa: شیر در بریتانیا پاینتی فروخته می‌شود.

n3.speaker: priya
n3.text: Hiya! Can I help you? You look a bit lost!

translations.fa: سلام! کمکتون کنم؟ یه کم گم‌شده به نظر می‌رسید!

branches.suggestion: Are there any eggs?
Yes, please. Where's the washing-up liquid?

n4.speaker: priya
n4.text: Eggs are in aisle five. There aren't any free-range ones left, sorry.

translations.fa: تخم‌مرغ راهروی پنجه. ببخشید، تخم‌مرغ محلی دیگه نمونده.

branches.suggestion: That's OK. Normal eggs are fine.
Are there any big boxes?

n5.speaker: priya
n5.text: There are some boxes of twelve. And washing-up liquid is next to the bin bags.

translations.fa: جعبه‌های دوازده‌تایی هست. مایع ظرفشویی هم کنار کیسه‌زباله‌هاست.

branches.suggestion: Thanks for your help!
Brilliant, thank you so much.

cultureNote.en: British vs American: bin (UK) = trash can (US); rubbish = trash.
cultureNote.fa: bin (بریتانیا) = trash can؛ rubbish = trash.

n6.speaker: priya
n6.text: No worries! Is there anything else you need today?

translations.fa: خواهش می‌کنم! امروز چیز دیگه‌ای لازم دارید؟

branches.suggestion: No, that's everything.
Have you got any crisps?

cultureNote.en: British vs American: crisps (UK) = chips (US). In the UK, chips are hot fried potatoes, like fries.
cultureNote.fa: crisps (بریتانیا) = chips (آمریکا)؛ chips بریتانیا = fries.

n7.speaker: priya
n7.text: The self-checkouts are over there. Have a lovely day!

translations.fa: صندوق‌های سلف‌سرویس اونجان. روز خوبی داشته باشید!

n1.speaker: ryan
n1.text: Mum gave me forty quid for new trainers. Can you help me choose?

translations.fa: مامان چهل پوند داد برای کتونی نو. کمکم می‌کنی انتخاب کنم؟

branches.suggestion: Of course! What colour do you want?
Forty quid? Lucky you!

cultureNote.en: "Quid" is slang for pounds: "ten quid" = £10. It never takes an s!
cultureNote.fa: quid یعنی پوند در محاوره؛ هیچ‌وقت s نمی‌گیرد.

n2.speaker: ryan
n2.text: White, I think. These ones or those ones over there?

translations.fa: سفید، فکر کنم. این‌ها یا اون‌هایی که اونجان؟

branches.suggestion: Those ones are nicer.
These are cheaper.

n3.speaker: ryan
n3.text: Those are forty-five pounds. These are thirty-five. Hmm.

translations.fa: اون‌ها چهل‌وپنج پوندن. این‌ها سی‌وپنج. هوم.

branches.suggestion: These are cheaper and they look good.
branches.suggestionFa: این‌ها ارزون‌ترن و خوب به نظر میان.

branches.suggestion: Try those on first.
branches.suggestionFa: اول اون‌ها را بپوش امتحان کن.

n4.speaker: ryan
n4.text: Excuse me, can I try these in a size nine, please?

translations.fa: ببخشید، می‌شه این‌ها را سایز نه امتحان کنم؟

branches.suggestion: Good — you asked politely!
Is nine your size?

cultureNote.en: UK shoe sizes are different: UK 9 is about EU 43 or US 10.
cultureNote.fa: سایز کفش بریتانیا فرق دارد: ۹ بریتانیا حدود ۴۳ اروپاست.

n5.speaker: ryan
n5.text: They're a bit small. Have you got a bigger size? Ah, the tens are better.

translations.fa: یه کم کوچیکن. سایز بزرگ‌تر دارید؟ آه، ده بهتره.

branches.suggestion: Walk around. Are they comfortable?
Size ten is better, then.

n6.speaker: ryan
n6.text: Really comfy. And I've got five quid left for chips! Want some?

translations.fa: خیلی راحتن. و پنج پوند هم برای سیب‌زمینی سرخ‌کرده موند! می‌خوای؟

branches.suggestion: Yes! Chips with salt and vinegar!
branches.suggestionFa: آره! چیپس با نمک و سرکه!

branches.suggestion: Save your money, Ryan!

n7.speaker: ryan
n7.text: Nah, chips are life. Come on, the chippy's round the corner!

translations.fa: نه بابا، چیپس زندگیه. بیا، مغازهٔ فیش‌اند‌چیپس سر کوچه‌ست!

n1.speaker: weda
n1.text: I need to pop into the chemist, dear. Come with me?

translations.fa: باید یه سر برم داروخونه عزیزم. باهام میای؟

branches.suggestion: Sure. Are you OK, Nana?
What's a chemist?

cultureNote.en: British vs American: the chemist's (UK) = drugstore / pharmacy (US). Boots is the most famous one.
cultureNote.fa: chemist (بریتانیا) = pharmacy/drugstore (آمریکا).

n2.speaker: weda
n2.text: It's a pharmacy. I need some plasters and something for my cough.

translations.fa: داروخونه‌ست. یه کم چسب‌زخم لازم دارم و یه چیزی برای سرفه‌ام.

branches.suggestion: I can ask for you.
Let's find the plasters first.
branches.suggestionFa: بیاید اول چسب‌زخم را پیدا کنیم.

cultureNote.en: British vs American: plaster (UK) = Band-Aid (US).
cultureNote.fa: plaster (بریتانیا) = Band-Aid (آمریکا).

n3.speaker: weda
n3.text: Thank you, dear. Ask the lady: "Can you recommend something for a cough?"

translations.fa: ممنون عزیزم. از خانم بپرس: «می‌تونید یه چیزی برای سرفه پیشنهاد بدید؟»

branches.suggestion: Excuse me, can you recommend something for a cough?
branches.suggestionFa: ببخشید، می‌تونید یه چیزی برای سرفه پیشنهاد بدید؟

branches.suggestion: Hello, my nana needs cough medicine.
branches.suggestionFa: سلام، مادربزرگم داروی سرفه لازم داره.

n4.speaker: weda
n4.text: She says this syrup is good. Two spoons, three times a day.

translations.fa: می‌گه این شربت خوبه. دو قاشق، روزی سه بار.

branches.suggestion: Two spoons, three times a day. OK!
branches.suggestionFa: دو قاشق، روزی سه بار. باشه!

branches.suggestion: Does it taste nice?

n5.speaker: weda
n5.text: Horrible, probably! Ha. And some throat sweets. Honey and lemon.

translations.fa: احتمالاً افتضاح! ها. و یه کم آب‌نبات گلو. عسل و لیمو.

branches.suggestion: Honey and lemon is good for colds.
branches.suggestionFa: عسل و لیمو برای سرماخوردگی خوبه.

branches.suggestion: I hope you feel better soon.

n6.speaker: weda
n6.text: You're a treasure. Now, a cup of tea at the café? My treat!

translations.fa: تو یه گنجی. حالا یه فنجون چای توی کافه؟ مهمون من!

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Look at me! I'm running! I'm running really fast!

translations.fa: منو ببین! دارم می‌دوم! خیلی تند دارم می‌دوم!

branches.suggestion: You're very fast!
Careful! Don't fall over!

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: What's William doing? Is he eating sand again?

translations.fa: ویلیام داره چی کار می‌کنه؟ دوباره داره شن می‌خوره؟

branches.suggestion: No, he's playing on the slide.
branches.suggestionFa: نه، داره روی سرسره بازی می‌کنه.

branches.suggestion: He's sitting in the sandpit.

n3.speaker: william
n3.text: Wheee! I like the slide! Again!

translations.fa: ویییی! سرسره را دوست دارم! دوباره!

branches.suggestion: One more time, William!
He's having so much fun.

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: Push me on the swings, please! Higher! Higher!

translations.fa: لطفاً منو روی تاب هل بده! بالاتر! بالاتر!

branches.suggestion: I'm pushing! Hold on tight!
That's high enough, Nicola.

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Look! Those boys are flying a kite. And that dog is chasing the ducks!

translations.fa: ببین! اون پسرها دارن بادبادک هوا می‌کنن. و اون سگ داره اردک‌ها را دنبال می‌کنه!

branches.suggestion: The ducks are flying away!
Oh no, the dog is jumping in the pond!
branches.suggestionFa: ای وای، سگ داره می‌پره توی برکه!

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: Ha ha! He's all wet! Now his owner is shouting. "Biscuit! Come here!"

translations.fa: ها ها! خیس خیس شده! حالا صاحبش داره داد می‌زنه. «بیسکویت! بیا اینجا!»

branches.suggestion: Is it Mrs Patel's dog?
Biscuit is a popular name here!

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: It's starting to rain! Quick, everyone's running home! Let's go!

translations.fa: داره بارون میگیره! زود، همه دارن می‌دون خونه! بریم!

n1.speaker: ryan
n1.text: Can you play football? Come on, we need one more player.

translations.fa: فوتبال بلدی؟ بیا، یه بازیکن دیگه لازم داریم.

branches.suggestion: Yes, I can play a bit.
No, I can't, but I can try!
branches.suggestionFa: نه، بلد نیستم، ولی می‌تونم امتحان کنم!

cultureNote.en: British vs American: football (UK) = soccer (US). American football is a different game.
cultureNote.fa: football (بریتانیا) = soccer (آمریکا).

n2.speaker: ryan
n2.text: Nice. Can you go in goal? Our keeper is rubbish.

translations.fa: عالی. می‌تونی دروازه‌بان باشی؟ دروازه‌بانمون افتضاحه.

branches.suggestion: OK, I can be the goalkeeper.
I can't catch very well.

n3.speaker: ryan
n3.text: Ha, no stress. Can you run fast? I can't — too many chips!

translations.fa: ها، استرس نداره. سریع می‌تونی بدوی؟ من نمی‌تونم — زیادی چیپس می‌خورم!

branches.suggestion: I can run quite fast.
Ha! Fewer chips, Ryan!

n4.speaker: ryan
n4.text: Can you speak other languages? You speak Farsi, right?

translations.fa: زبان‌های دیگه بلدی؟ فارسی بلدی، نه؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I can speak Farsi and English.
I can speak a little Arabic too.

n5.speaker: ryan
n5.text: That's sick! I can only speak English. And a bit of French. "Bonjour!"

translations.fa: خیلی باحاله! من فقط انگلیسی بلدم. و یه کم فرانسوی. «بونژور!»

branches.suggestion: Can you teach me some slang?
branches.suggestionFa: می‌تونی یه کم اصطلاح عامیانه یادم بدی؟

branches.suggestion: I can teach you some Farsi!
branches.suggestionFa: من می‌تونم یه کم فارسی یادت بدم!

cultureNote.en: Teenagers use "sick" to mean great. Your teacher won't say it!
cultureNote.fa: نوجوان‌ها «sick» را به معنای عالی می‌گویند.

n6.speaker: ryan
n6.text: Deal! "Sick" means great, "peng" means really nice. Now, can you score?

translations.fa: قبول! «sick» یعنی عالی، «peng» یعنی خیلی خوب. حالا گل می‌تونی بزنی؟

branches.suggestion: I can try. Pass me the ball!
branches.suggestionFa: می‌تونم امتحان کنم. توپ را پاس بده!

branches.suggestion: Watch this! Goal!

n7.speaker: ryan
n7.text: Get in! What a goal! You can definitely play. Same time next week?

translations.fa: ایول! چه گلی! قطعاً بلدی بازی کنی. هفتهٔ بعد همین ساعت؟

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Hi love, it's me. Are you at home? What are you doing?

translations.fa: سلام عزیزم، منم. خونه‌ای؟ داری چی کار می‌کنی؟

branches.suggestion: I'm watching telly.
I'm cooking dinner.

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: Lovely. Is Ryan doing his homework? Can you check?

translations.fa: چه خوب. رایان داره تکلیفش را انجام می‌ده؟ می‌تونی چک کنی؟

branches.suggestion: No, he's playing video games.
Yes, he's working in his room.
branches.suggestionFa: آره، داره توی اتاقش کار می‌کنه.

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: I knew it! Tell him to turn it off. What's Nicola doing?

translations.fa: می‌دونستم! بهش بگو خاموشش کنه. نیکولا چی کار می‌کنه؟

branches.suggestion: She's drawing a picture.
She's reading with Nana.

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: Aw. And William? He's being very quiet. Too quiet…

translations.fa: آخی. ویلیام چی؟ خیلی ساکته. زیادی ساکت…

branches.suggestion: He's sleeping on the sofa.
Oh no. He's painting the wall!
branches.suggestionFa: ای وای. داره دیوار را رنگ می‌کنه!

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: Oh, he's sleeping! Thank goodness. I'm waiting for the bus now. It's late, as usual.

translations.fa: آه، خوابیده! خدا را شکر. الان منتظر اتوبوسم. طبق معمول دیر کرده.

branches.suggestion: Is it raining there?
Shall I put the kettle on?

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: Yes please, love! I'm getting on the bus now. See you in twenty minutes!

translations.fa: آره لطفاً عزیزم! الان دارم سوار اتوبوس می‌شم. بیست دقیقه دیگه می‌بینمت!

n1.speaker: tom
n1.text: Can you give me a hand? I'm putting up a shelf.

translations.fa: می‌تونی کمکم کنی؟ دارم یه قفسه نصب می‌کنم.

branches.suggestion: Sure. What can I do?
Can you do DIY, Tom?

cultureNote.en: DIY = "do it yourself": fixing and building things at home. Very popular in Britain.
cultureNote.fa: DIY یعنی «خودت انجامش بده»: تعمیر و ساخت در خانه.

n2.speaker: tom
n2.text: Can you hold this end? Keep it straight. Is it straight?

translations.fa: می‌تونی این سرش را نگه داری؟ صاف نگهش دار. صافه؟

branches.suggestion: No, it's a bit high on the left.
branches.suggestionFa: نه، سمت چپ یه کم بالاست.

branches.suggestion: Yes, it looks straight to me.

n3.speaker: tom
n3.text: Hmm. Can you pass me the drill? It's in the toolbox.

translations.fa: هوم. می‌تونی دریل را بدی؟ توی جعبه ابزاره.

branches.suggestion: Here's the drill.
Is this the drill or a hammer?

n4.speaker: tom
n4.text: That's the drill. Right — I'm drilling now. Cover your ears!

translations.fa: اون دریله. خب — دارم دریل می‌کنم. گوش‌هات را بگیر!

branches.suggestion: It's very loud!
Careful, Tom! Is William nearby?

n5.speaker: tom
n5.text: Leslie's got him in the garden. Now, can you pass the screws?

translations.fa: لزلی توی باغچه نگهش داشته. حالا، پیچ‌ها را می‌دی؟

branches.suggestion: Here are the screws. How many?
I can't see any screws.

n6.speaker: tom
n6.text: Four. There! Look at that! Is it falling down? No! It's perfect!

translations.fa: چهارتا. ایناهاش! ببین! داره می‌افته؟ نه! عالیه!

branches.suggestion: Well done! It looks great.
Er, Tom… it's moving a bit.
branches.suggestionFa: اِم، تام… یه کم داره تکون می‌خوره.

n7.speaker: tom
n7.text: Moving? No, no. It's fine. Let's get a cuppa before it falls down!

translations.fa: تکون؟ نه، نه. خوبه. بیا قبل از اینکه بیفته یه چای بخوریم!

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Let's sing! Head, shoulders, knees and toes! Touch your head!

translations.fa: بیا آواز بخونیم! سر، شونه، زانو و انگشت پا! سرت را لمس کن!

branches.suggestion: I'm touching my head!
Is this a song from school?

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: Yes! Now touch your nose. And your ears. Faster!

translations.fa: آره! حالا دماغت را لمس کن. و گوش‌هات. تندتر!

branches.suggestion: Nose, ears… oops, that's my mouth!
I'm too slow!

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: Ha ha! How many fingers have you got? I've got ten!

translations.fa: ها ها! چندتا انگشت داری؟ من ده‌تا دارم!

branches.suggestion: I've got ten fingers too.
Ten fingers and ten toes!
branches.suggestionFa: ده انگشت دست و ده انگشت پا!

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: William's got a big tummy. Look! Tickle tickle!

translations.fa: ویلیام یه شکم گنده داره. ببین! قلقلک قلقلک!

branches.suggestion: Where's William's tummy?
Gently, Nicola!

n5.speaker: william
n5.text: No! Don't tickle me! Ha ha!

translations.fa: نه! قلقلکم نده! ها ها!

branches.suggestion: He's laughing so much!
Tickle his feet too!

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: Ow! I banged my knee on the table. It hurts!

translations.fa: آخ! زانوم خورد به میز. درد می‌کنه!

branches.suggestion: Let me see. Where does it hurt?
Oh no! Shall I get your mum?
branches.suggestionFa: ای وای! مامانت را صدا کنم؟

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: Here. It's a bit red. Can I have a plaster with a dinosaur on it?

translations.fa: اینجا. یه کم قرمزه. می‌شه یه چسب زخم دایناسوری داشته باشم؟

branches.suggestion: Here's a dinosaur plaster. Better?
branches.suggestionFa: بفرما یه چسب زخم دایناسوری. بهتره؟

branches.suggestion: Let's put some ice on it first.
branches.suggestionFa: بیا اول یه کم یخ بذاریم روش.

n8.speaker: nicola
n8.text: All better! Dinosaur plasters are magic. Again! Head, shoulders, knees and toes!

translations.fa: خوب شد! چسب‌های دایناسوری جادویی‌ان. دوباره! سر، شونه، زانو و انگشت پا!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Oh love, you look pale. Are you feeling poorly?

translations.fa: آه عزیزم، رنگت پریده. حالت خوب نیست؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I feel terrible.
I'm OK, just a bit tired.

cultureNote.en: Brits say "poorly" or "under the weather" for feeling ill. Americans say "sick".
cultureNote.fa: بریتانیایی‌ها «poorly» یا «under the weather» می‌گویند.

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: What's the matter? Have you got a headache?

translations.fa: چی شده؟ سردرد داری؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I've got a bad headache.
No, I've got a sore throat.

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: Let me feel your forehead. You're very hot. I think you've got a temperature.

translations.fa: بذار پیشونیت را ببینم. خیلی داغی. فکر کنم تب داری.

branches.suggestion: I feel hot and cold.
Have you got a thermometer?

cultureNote.en: Brits say "I've got a temperature" to mean a fever.
cultureNote.fa: «I've got a temperature» یعنی تب دارم.

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: Thirty-eight point five. That's a temperature, all right. Have you got a cough?

translations.fa: سی‌وهشت و نیم. تبه دیگه. سرفه هم داری؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, and a runny nose.
No cough, but my body aches.
branches.suggestionFa: سرفه نه، ولی بدنم درد می‌کنه.

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: Sounds like flu. Go to bed. I'll bring you some paracetamol and a hot drink.

translations.fa: به نظر آنفولانزاست. برو بخواب. برات پاراستامول و یه نوشیدنی گرم میارم.

branches.suggestion: Thank you. You're very kind.
Can I have honey and lemon?

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: Of course. Drink lots of water and rest. If you're worse tomorrow, we'll call the GP.

translations.fa: البته. زیاد آب بخور و استراحت کن. اگه فردا بدتر بودی، به دکتر عمومی زنگ می‌زنیم.

branches.suggestion: What's a GP?
OK. I'll rest today.

cultureNote.en: GP = General Practitioner, your local family doctor. You register with a GP surgery near your home.
