n4.speaker: ryan
n4.text: Blue is full fat. Next: eggs, bread, washing-up liquid… I can't find the washing-up liquid!

translations.fa: آبی پرچربه. بعدی: تخم‌مرغ، نون، مایع ظرفشویی… مایع ظرفشویی را پیدا نمی‌کنم!

branches.suggestion: It's in the cleaning aisle.
Ask the staff.

n5.speaker: priya
n5.text: Washing-up liquid? Aisle nine, with the cleaning products. Anything else?

translations.fa: مایع ظرفشویی؟ راهروی نه، کنار مواد شوینده. چیز دیگه؟

branches.suggestion: We can't find the gravy.
Have you seen the custard?

recasts.echo: You can't find the gravy? Aisle three!

n6.speaker: priya
n6.text: Gravy and custard are both in aisle three. Next to the stock cubes.

translations.fa: گریوی و کاستارد هر دو راهروی سه‌ان. کنار عصاره‌ها.

branches.suggestion: Thanks a lot.
Aisle three. Easy!

n7.speaker: ryan
n7.text: You're a lifesaver. Last thing: "something nice for Mum". What does that mean?

translations.fa: تو نجات‌دهنده‌ای. آخرین چیز: «یه چیز خوب برای مامان». یعنی چی؟

branches.suggestion: Buy her some flowers.
Chocolate!

n8.speaker: ryan
n8.text: Flowers AND chocolate. Then she'll forget I broke the remote. Don't tell her!

translations.fa: گل و شکلات. اون وقت یادش میره کنترل را شکستم. بهش نگو!

n1.speaker: priya
n1.text: Hi again! Oh, who's this little one?

translations.fa: دوباره سلام! آه، این کوچولو کیه؟

branches.suggestion: This is Nicola. Is there a toilet here?
Sorry, it's urgent. Where's the toilet?

cultureNote.en: British "toilet" or "loo", American "restroom" or "bathroom".
cultureNote.fa: toilet/loo/restroom.

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: I need a wee! Now!

translations.fa: جیش دارم! همین الان!

branches.suggestion: Quick, Nicola!
Hold on, we're going!
branches.suggestionFa: یه کم صبر کن، داریم میریم!

n3.speaker: priya
n3.text: Customer toilets are at the back, past the bakery. Then turn left.

translations.fa: دستشویی مشتری‌ها ته فروشگاهه، بعد از نونوایی. بعد بپیچ چپ.

branches.suggestion: Past the bakery, then left.
Is it far?

n4.speaker: priya
n4.text: Not far. Thirty seconds! There's a code on the door. It's one-two-three-four.

translations.fa: دور نیست. سی ثانیه! رو در یه رمز هست. یک-دو-سه-چهار.

branches.suggestion: A code? OK, one-two-three-four.
Is there a baby-changing room too?

n5.speaker: priya
n5.text: Yes, next to the toilets. Hurry!

translations.fa: آره، کنار دستشویی‌ها. عجله کنید!

branches.suggestion: Come on, Nicola. Run!
Thank you!

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: Made it! Phew! Can I wash my hands? Is there soap?

translations.fa: رسیدیم! آخیش! می‌تونم دستام را بشورم؟ صابون هست؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, there's soap by the sink.
Is there a hand dryer?

recasts.echo: Is there soap? Yes, by the sink.

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: The dryer is SO loud! I'm scared! Can I use paper towels?

translations.fa: خشک‌کن خیلی بلنده! می‌ترسم! می‌تونم دستمال کاغذی استفاده کنم؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, here's a paper towel.
It's OK. It's only noisy.

n8.speaker: priya
n8.text: All better? Here's a sticker for being so quick! Mind how you go!

translations.fa: همه چی خوبه؟ اینم یه برچسب برای این‌همه سرعت! مواظب خودتون باشید!

n1.speaker: ryan
n1.text: Whoa! Your bag broke! Oranges everywhere! Quick, grab them!

translations.fa: وای! کیسه‌ت پاره شد! پرتقال همه جا! سریع، برشون دار!

branches.suggestion: Oh no! Can you help me?
Sorry, everyone!

n2.speaker: ryan
n2.text: One's rolling under the shelf! Got it!

translations.fa: یکی داره زیر قفسه قل می‌خوره! گرفتمش!

branches.suggestion: Thank you so much, Ryan!
Good catch!

n3.speaker: priya
n3.text: Oh dear! Don't worry. Here's a new bag. A strong one. No charge.

translations.fa: ای وای! نگران نباشید. اینم یه کیسهٔ نو. محکم. مجانی.

branches.suggestion: That's really kind of you.
Thank you. That's very kind.

cultureNote.en: UK shops charge for carrier bags, so a free bag is a nice gesture.
cultureNote.fa: کیسهٔ پولی در فروشگاه.

recasts.echo: That's kind? It's nothing!

n4.speaker: priya
n4.text: No problem at all. It happens every day! Are any of them squashed?

translations.fa: اصلاً مشکلی نیست. هر روز پیش میاد! هیچ‌کدومشون له شده؟

branches.suggestion: This one is a bit squashed.
branches.suggestionFa: این یکی یه کم له شده.

branches.suggestion: No, they're all fine.

n5.speaker: priya
n5.text: Let me change it for a new one. There you go. Good as new!

translations.fa: بذار با یه نو عوضش کنم. بفرما. مثل روز اول!

branches.suggestion: You're a star. Thank you.
Thanks, I really appreciate it.

n6.speaker: ryan
n6.text: Ha! "I really appreciate it." Very posh. You sound like the King!

translations.fa: ها! «واقعاً قدردانم.» خیلی اعیونی. مثل شاه حرف می‌زنی!

branches.suggestion: Is that too formal?
What do you say, then?

n7.speaker: ryan
n7.text: It's fine! I just say "Cheers" or "Ta". Thanks, Priya — cheers!

translations.fa: خوبه! من فقط میگم «چیرز» یا «تا». ممنون پریا — چیرز!

branches.suggestion: Cheers, Priya!
Ta!

cultureNote.en: "Cheers" and "ta" are informal British ways to say thank you.
cultureNote.fa: cheers و ta یعنی ممنون.

n8.speaker: priya
n8.text: Ha! Any time, boys. Next time, use two bags for oranges. They're heavy!

translations.fa: ها! هر وقت خواستید، پسرها. دفعهٔ بعد برای پرتقال دو تا کیسه بگیرید. سنگینن!

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Look! I broke my piggy bank! Can you help me count my money?

translations.fa: ببین! قلکم را شکستم! کمکم می‌کنی پولم را بشمرم؟

branches.suggestion: Of course! Let's count.
Wow, lots of coins!

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: What's this little brown one?

translations.fa: این کوچیکهٔ قهوه‌ای چیه؟

branches.suggestion: That's a penny. One p.
It's one pence.

cultureNote.en: British people say "p" for pence: "20p" = "twenty p". 100p = £1.
cultureNote.fa: p یعنی پنی.

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: And this big silver one? It has seven sides!

translations.fa: و این بزرگه نقره‌ای؟ هفت تا ضلع داره!

branches.suggestion: That's fifty p.
Count the sides with me!

cultureNote.en: The 20p and 50p coins have seven sides, and the £1 coin has twelve.
cultureNote.fa: سکه‌های هفت‌ضلعی.

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: Seven! And the gold one?

translations.fa: هفت تا! و طلاییه؟

branches.suggestion: That's a pound. A one-pound coin.
branches.suggestionFa: اون یه پونده. سکهٔ یک پوندی.

branches.suggestion: The two-pound coin is gold and silver.
branches.suggestionFa: سکهٔ دو پوندی طلایی و نقره‌ایه.

recasts.echo: One pound? Yes!

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: I've got a note too! Nana gave me it. It's purple. Is it a lot?

translations.fa: یه اسکناس هم دارم! نانا بهم داد. بنفشه. زیاده؟

branches.suggestion: That's a twenty-pound note!
Wow, Nicola. You're rich!

cultureNote.en: British notes: £5 is blue-green, £10 orange, £20 purple, £50 red.
cultureNote.fa: رنگ اسکناس‌ها.

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: Rich! OK, let's put them in piles. Pennies here, pounds there.

translations.fa: پولدار! باشه، بیا دسته‌شون کنیم. پنی‌ها اینجا، پوندها اونجا.

branches.suggestion: Ten pennies make ten p.
branches.suggestionFa: ده تا پنی میشه ده پی.

branches.suggestion: I've got four pound coins here.
branches.suggestionFa: اینجا چهار تا سکهٔ پوندی دارم.

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: So how much is it altogether? Is it a hundred pounds?

translations.fa: پس جمعاً چقدره؟ صد پونده؟

branches.suggestion: No, it's twenty-six pounds fifty.
branches.suggestionFa: نه، بیست و شش پوند و پنجاه پی.

branches.suggestion: Let me add it up.

n8.speaker: nicola
n8.text: Twenty-six pounds fifty! I can buy a unicorn! Or two! Or a pony!

translations.fa: بیست و شش پوند و پنجاه! می‌تونم یه تک‌شاخ بخرم! یا دو تا! یا یه اسب کوچولو!

n1.speaker: baker
n1.text: Good morning! Busy day. What can I get you?

translations.fa: صبح بخیر! روز شلوغیه. چی بدم خدمتتون؟

branches.suggestion: How much is the apple pie?
How much are the doughnuts?

recasts.echo: How much are the doughnuts? Ninety p each!

n2.speaker: baker
n2.text: The apple pie is five pounds fifty. The doughnuts are ninety p each.

translations.fa: پای سیب پنج پوند و پنجاهه. دونات‌ها هر کدوم نود پی.

branches.suggestion: Ninety p each. That's cheap.
And how much is a cup of tea?

n3.speaker: baker
n3.text: Tea is one pound twenty. Coffee is two pounds forty.

translations.fa: چای یک پوند و بیست. قهوه دو پوند و چهل.

branches.suggestion: One pound twenty.
Coffee is double the price!

cultureNote.en: Prices are said simply: "£1.20" is "one pound twenty" or "one twenty".
cultureNote.fa: خواندن قیمت.

n4.speaker: baker
n4.text: Ha, good maths! Coffee beans are expensive. And sausage rolls are on offer: three for two pounds.

translations.fa: ها، ریاضیت خوبه! دونهٔ قهوه گرونه. و سوسیس‌رول‌ها حراجن: سه تا دو پوند.

branches.suggestion: What's a sausage roll?
Three, please!

cultureNote.en: A sausage roll is sausage meat in pastry. Most bakeries also sell vegetarian ones.
cultureNote.fa: سوسیس‌رول.

n5.speaker: baker
n5.text: Sausage meat in pastry. We do vegan ones too. How many would you like?

translations.fa: گوشت سوسیس تو خمیر. وگان هم داریم. چند تا می‌خواید؟

branches.suggestion: Two vegan ones, please.
Three. How much is that?

n6.speaker: baker
n6.text: The offer is any three for two pounds. Mix and match!

translations.fa: تخفیف برای هر سه تایی دو پونده. قاطی هم میشه!

branches.suggestion: Then three, please. And a tea.
branches.suggestionFa: پس سه تا، لطفاً. و یه چای.

branches.suggestion: How much is it altogether?

n7.speaker: baker
n7.text: Three sausage rolls and a tea. That's three pounds twenty, please.

translations.fa: سه تا سوسیس‌رول و یه چای. میشه سه پوند و بیست، لطفاً.

branches.suggestion: Here's three pounds twenty.
Can I pay by card?

n8.speaker: baker
n8.text: Perfect. Thank you! The sausage rolls are hot, so be careful. Enjoy!

translations.fa: عالی. ممنون! سوسیس‌رول‌ها داغن، پس مواظب باشید. نوش جان!

n1.speaker: ryan
n1.text: Guess what? I've got a Saturday job! At the bakery. Will you be my first customer?

translations.fa: حدس بزن چی شده؟ کار شنبه‌ها گرفتم! تو نونوایی. اولین مشتری‌م میشی؟

branches.suggestion: Of course! I'll buy a loaf.
A job? Well done, Ryan!

cultureNote.en: In the UK, teenagers from 13 can do light part-time work, like a Saturday job, for a few hours.
cultureNote.fa: کار نیمه‌وقت نوجوانان.

n2.speaker: ryan
n2.text: Thanks! OK… one white loaf. That's one pound eighty.

translations.fa: ممنون! باشه… یه نون سفید. میشه یک پوند و هشتاد.

branches.suggestion: Here's a five-pound note.
Here's two pounds.

n3.speaker: ryan
n3.text: Two pounds. So your change is… twenty p! Here you go.

translations.fa: دو پوند. پس بقیه‌ش… بیست پی! بفرما.

branches.suggestion: Thank you.
Is that right? Let me check.

n4.speaker: baker
n4.text: Good, Ryan. Always count the change back. Out loud. Try a harder one.

translations.fa: خوبه رایان. همیشه بقیهٔ پول را بلند بشمر. یه سخت‌ترش را امتحان کن.

branches.suggestion: OK. Two doughnuts, please.
A cake and a coffee, please.
branches.suggestionFa: یه کیک و یه قهوه، لطفاً.

n5.speaker: ryan
n5.text: A cake and a coffee. Three fifty plus two forty… five pounds ninety.

translations.fa: یه کیک و یه قهوه. سه و پنجاه به اضافهٔ دو و چهل… پنج پوند و نود.

branches.suggestion: Here's a ten-pound note.
I've only got a twenty. Sorry!

n6.speaker: ryan
n6.text: From ten. So… five ninety, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. Four pounds ten change!

translations.fa: از ده. پس… پنج و نود، شش، هفت، هشت، نه، ده. چهار پوند و ده بقیه!

branches.suggestion: Perfect! Four pounds ten.
That's clever, counting up.

match: my change is four pound and ten
recasts.echo: Four pounds ten? Spot on!
recasts.better: My change is four pounds ten.
recasts.betterFa: بقیهٔ پولم چهار پوند و ده‌ئه.

n7.speaker: baker
n7.text: Spot on! You're a natural. Now, the hard part — smile at every customer!

translations.fa: دقیقاً! ذاتی بلدی. حالا قسمت سخت — به هر مشتری لبخند بزن!

branches.suggestion: Ha! Smile, Ryan!
He's a teenager. Smiling is hard!

n8.speaker: ryan
n8.text: Ha ha, very funny. See? I'm smiling. Have a nice day, sir! Next customer, please!

translations.fa: ها ها، خیلی بامزه. دیدی؟ دارم لبخند می‌زنم. روز خوبی داشته باشید قربان! مشتری بعدی، لطفاً!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Nicola wants to spend all her money on sweets! I'm trying to teach her to save.

translations.fa: نیکولا می‌خواد همهٔ پولش را خرج آبنبات کنه! دارم سعی می‌کنم پس‌انداز کردن را یادش بدم.

branches.suggestion: How much pocket money does she get?
Saving is hard for kids.

cultureNote.en: British "pocket money", American "allowance".
cultureNote.fa: pocket money/allowance.

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: Two pounds a week. For tidying her room. Nicola, what do you want to buy?

translations.fa: هفته‌ای دو پوند. برای مرتب کردن اتاقش. نیکولا، می‌خوای چی بخری؟

branches.suggestion: What do you want, Nicola?
Is it a toy?

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: A big unicorn from the toy shop! It's fifteen pounds. And sweets. Today!

translations.fa: یه تک‌شاخ بزرگ از اسباب‌بازی‌فروشی! پونزده پونده. و آبنبات. امروز!

branches.suggestion: Then you need to save up.
Sweets or unicorn? Choose one!
branches.suggestionFa: آبنبات یا تک‌شاخ؟ یکی را انتخاب کن!

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: Exactly. If you save two pounds every week, how many weeks?

translations.fa: دقیقاً. اگه هر هفته دو پوند پس‌انداز کنی، چند هفته میشه؟

branches.suggestion: Fifteen divided by two…
About eight weeks.

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Eight weeks?! That's forever! I need sweets now!

translations.fa: هشت هفته؟! این یعنی یه عمر! الان آبنبات لازم دارم!

branches.suggestion: You don't need sweets. You want sweets!
Just one small bag?

recasts.echo: She needs to save? Exactly!

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: Good point! What about this: fifty p for sweets, one pound fifty in the piggy bank?

translations.fa: نکتهٔ خوبیه! این چطوره: پنجاه پی برای آبنبات، یک پوند و پنجاه تو قلک؟

branches.suggestion: That's a fair idea.
Then it's ten weeks.

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: Ten weeks… OK. But can I help {you} with jobs? For extra money?

translations.fa: ده هفته… باشه. ولی می‌تونم تو کارها به {you} کمک کنم؟ برای پول اضافه؟

branches.suggestion: You can water my plants!
Ask Mummy first.

n8.speaker: leslie
n8.text: Ha! A little businesswoman. Fine — fifty p for watering. Just don't flood his kitchen!

translations.fa: ها! یه تاجر کوچولو. باشه — پنجاه پی برای آب دادن. فقط آشپزخونه‌ش را آب نبر!

l1_u45_1.title: I can swim
l1_u45_1.setting: Saying what you can do · Level 1

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Look at the lido! It opens next week. Can you swim, {you}?

translations.fa: استخر روباز را ببین! هفتهٔ بعد باز میشه. شنا بلدی {you}؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I can swim.
I can swim a bit.

cultureNote.en: A "lido" is an outdoor public swimming pool. London Fields Lido in Hackney is open all year!
cultureNote.fa: لیدو استخر روباز.

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: Great! Can you swim well?

translations.fa: عالی! خوب شنا می‌کنی؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I can swim very well.
Not very well. I can't swim far.
branches.suggestionFa: نه خیلی خوب. نمی‌تونم زیاد شنا کنم.

recasts.echo: You can swim? Brilliant!

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: Where did you swim in Iran? Tehran isn't by the sea, is it?

translations.fa: تو ایران کجا شنا می‌کردی؟ تهران کنار دریا نیست، نه؟

branches.suggestion: Yes! In summer we go to the Caspian Sea.
The sea is far from Tehran.

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: How lovely. The lido is cold, though. Can you swim in cold water?

translations.fa: چه قشنگ. ولی استخر روباز سرده. تو آب سرد می‌تونی شنا کنی؟

branches.suggestion: No, I can't! I like warm water.
branches.suggestionFa: نه، نمی‌تونم! آب گرم دوست دارم.

branches.suggestion: How cold is it?

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: Sometimes eighteen degrees! Tom can't swim in cold water. He screams!

translations.fa: گاهی هجده درجه! تام نمی‌تونه تو آب سرد شنا کنه. جیغ می‌زنه!

branches.suggestion: Ha! Can Tom swim well?
Eighteen degrees is very cold!

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: Tom can swim, but he can't dive. He jumps in like a big rock! Splash!

translations.fa: تام شنا بلده، ولی شیرجه نمی‌تونه. مثل یه سنگ بزرگ می‌پره تو! شالاپ!

branches.suggestion: Can you dive, Leslie?
I can't dive either.

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: I can! I was in the swimming team at school. Ryan can swim really fast too.

translations.fa: بلدم! تو مدرسه عضو تیم شنا بودم. رایان هم واقعاً تند شنا می‌کنه.

branches.suggestion: Can Nicola swim?
Let's all go together!

n8.speaker: leslie
n8.text: Nicola can swim with armbands. Let's go on Saturday! Bring a towel and a brave face!

translations.fa: نیکولا با بازوبند شنا می‌کنه. شنبه بریم! یه حوله و یه چهرهٔ شجاع بیار!

l1_u45_2.title: Can you ride a bike?
l1_u45_2.setting: Saying what you can do · Level 1

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Look! I've got a new bike! It's pink! Can you ride a bike?

translations.fa: ببین! دوچرخهٔ جدید دارم! صورتیه! تو دوچرخه‌سواری بلدی؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I can.
Yes, but not very well.

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: I can't ride without my stabilisers. Daddy says they're coming off today!

translations.fa: من بدون چرخ کمکی نمی‌تونم برونم. بابا میگه امروز درشون میاره!

branches.suggestion: Are you scared?
You can do it, Nicola!

cultureNote.en: British "stabilisers", American "training wheels".
cultureNote.fa: stabilisers/training wheels.

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: A bit scared. Can you hold the back of my seat?

translations.fa: یه کم می‌ترسم. می‌تونی پشت صندلیم را بگیری؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I can hold it.
Of course. I won't let go.

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: OK. Can I wear my helmet with the stars?

translations.fa: باشه. می‌تونم کلاه ایمنی ستاره‌دارم را بذارم؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, you can. Safety first!
Can you do the strap?

recasts.echo: Can you wear it? Of course!

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Ready! Push! Push! Are you still holding?

translations.fa: آماده! هل بده! هل بده! هنوز گرفتی؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I'm holding.
Pedal, Nicola, pedal!

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: Wheee! Look! I can ride! Are you holding? … You're NOT holding!

translations.fa: وییی! ببین! می‌تونم برونم! داری می‌گیری؟ … نمی‌گیری!

branches.suggestion: You're doing it by yourself!
I let go! You can ride!

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: I CAN RIDE A BIKE! All by myself! Can Mr Buttons sit in the basket?

translations.fa: دوچرخه‌سواری بلدم! خودم تنهایی! آقای دکمه می‌تونه تو سبد بشینه؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, he can.
Can he hold on tight?

n8.speaker: nicola
n8.text: He can! Can we race now? You run, I ride. Ready, steady, GO!

translations.fa: می‌تونه! حالا می‌تونیم مسابقه بدیم؟ تو بدو، من رکاب می‌زنم. حاضر، آماده، برو!

l1_u45_3.title: I can't whistle
l1_u45_3.setting: Saying what you can do · Level 1

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Listen to that bird! I wish I could whistle. I can't whistle at all! Can you?

translations.fa: به اون پرنده گوش کن! کاش سوت زدن بلد بودم. اصلاً نمی‌تونم سوت بزنم! تو می‌تونی؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I can whistle. Listen!
No, I can't whistle either.

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: Teach me! I'm bad at it. I just blow air. Pfff!

translations.fa: یادم بده! تو این کار بدم. فقط باد میدم. پففف!

branches.suggestion: Make your lips small, like an O.
branches.suggestionFa: لب‌هات را کوچیک کن، مثل یه O.

branches.suggestion: Ha! That's not a whistle.

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: Like an O… Pfff… Phweet! Was that it?

translations.fa: مثل یه O… پففف… فیییت! همین بود؟

branches.suggestion: Yes! You're getting good at it!
Almost! Try again.

recasts.echo: You're good at it? Thank you!

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: Ha! OK, your turn. What can't you do? Everyone has something!

translations.fa: ها! خب، نوبت توئه. تو چی بلد نیستی؟ هر کسی یه چیزی داره!

branches.suggestion: I can't sing. I'm terrible!
I can't cook British food.

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: Everyone can sing! Can you sing a Persian song for me? Just a little one?

translations.fa: همه می‌تونن بخونن! می‌تونی برام یه آهنگ فارسی بخونی؟ فقط یه کوچولو؟

branches.suggestion: No way! Not in the park!
OK, but don't laugh!

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: I won't laugh! … That was beautiful! You're good at singing!

translations.fa: نمی‌خندم! … قشنگ بود! تو آواز خوندن خوبی!

branches.suggestion: Thank you! I'm still bad at whistling.
branches.suggestionFa: ممنون! ولی هنوز تو سوت بدم.

branches.suggestion: Can you sing, Leslie?

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Only in the car! Tom says I sound like a fox. You practise whistling, I'll practise singing!

translations.fa: فقط تو ماشین! تام میگه صدام مثل روباهه. تو سوت تمرین کن، منم آواز!

l1_u45_4.title: Nicola can skip
l1_u45_4.setting: Saying what you can do · Level 1

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Look what I can do! I can skip! With a rope! Watch me!

translations.fa: ببین چی کار بلدم! طناب‌بازی بلدم! با طناب! نگام کن!

branches.suggestion: Wow! How many can you do?
I'm watching!

cultureNote.en: British "skipping rope", American "jump rope".
cultureNote.fa: skipping/jump rope.

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: One, two, three, four… oops! Four! I can do four. Can you skip?

translations.fa: یک، دو، سه، چهار… اوپس! چهار! چهار تا بلدم. تو طناب‌بازی بلدی؟

branches.suggestion: Let me try.
I can't skip with a rope.

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: Everybody can skip! Here. Jump when the rope goes under your feet!

translations.fa: همه بلدن! بیا. وقتی طناب از زیر پات رد شد بپر!

branches.suggestion: One, two, three… ouch!
I did ten!

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: Ha ha! Mia can do twenty. She can skip for a whole minute!

translations.fa: ها ها! میا بیست تا بلده. یه دقیقهٔ کامل طناب می‌زنه!

branches.suggestion: Twenty? Mia is very good!
Can you do twenty one day?
branches.suggestionFa: یه روز می‌تونی بیست تا بزنی؟

recasts.echo: Mia can skip? Yes, really well!
recasts.better: Mia can skip for a minute.

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Yes! If I practise. Can I do a cartwheel too? Watch!

translations.fa: آره! اگه تمرین کنم. می‌تونم چرخ و فلک هم بزنم؟ نگاه کن!

branches.suggestion: Be careful, Nicola!
Wow! What's that?

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: A cartwheel! Hands, hands, feet, feet! Can you do a cartwheel?

translations.fa: چرخ و فلک! دست، دست، پا، پا! تو بلدی؟

branches.suggestion: No! I'm too old!
I can try, but I can't promise!
branches.suggestionFa: می‌تونم امتحان کنم، ولی قول نمیدم!

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: You're not old! Nana is old. She can't do cartwheels, but she can knit!

translations.fa: تو پیر نیستی! نانا پیره. نمی‌تونه چرخ و فلک بزنه، ولی می‌تونه بافتنی ببافه!

branches.suggestion: Everyone can do something.
Can you knit, Nicola?

n8.speaker: nicola
n8.text: Not yet! Nana's teaching me. Next week I can show you a scarf. A very, very small scarf!

translations.fa: هنوز نه! نانا داره یادم میده. هفتهٔ بعد بهت یه شال‌گردن نشون میدم. یه شال‌گردن خیلی خیلی کوچیک!

n1.speaker: tom
n1.text: Ah, you're here! Come in, come in! And Mrs Khan too. Lovely!

translations.fa: آه، اومدید! بیاید تو، بیاید تو! و خانم خان هم. عالی!

branches.suggestion: Hi, Tom. Thanks for inviting us.
branches.suggestionFa: سلام تام. ممنون که دعوتمون کردی.

branches.suggestion: Hello! Sorry we're a bit late.
branches.suggestionFa: سلام! ببخشید یه کم دیر کردیم.

n2.speaker: tom
n2.text: Late? Not at all! Leslie's still in the kitchen. Let me take your coats.

translations.fa: دیر؟ اصلاً! لزلی هنوز تو آشپزخونه‌ست. بذارید کتاتون را بگیرم.

branches.suggestion: Here you are. Thank you.
Where shall I put my umbrella?

n3.speaker: khan
n3.text: Thank you, Tom. I brought some samosas. Still warm!

translations.fa: ممنون تام. یه کم سمبوسه آوردم. هنوز گرمه!

branches.suggestion: They smell amazing!
I brought some sweets from the Persian shop.
branches.suggestionFa: منم از مغازهٔ ایرانی شیرینی آوردم.

cultureNote.en: In Britain it's polite to bring a small gift when you visit: flowers, chocolates, wine or something homemade.
cultureNote.fa: هدیهٔ کوچک برای میزبان.

n4.speaker: tom
n4.text: You shouldn't have! Leslie, they've brought food! Go through to the living room.

translations.fa: زحمت کشیدید! لزلی، غذا آوردن! بفرمایید به اتاق نشیمن.

branches.suggestion: Which way is it?
Thank you. After you, Mrs Khan.

cultureNote.en: "You shouldn't have!" is a polite way to say thank you for a gift — it doesn't mean "don't".
cultureNote.fa: تعارف انگلیسی.

n5.speaker: tom
n5.text: First door on the left. Sit anywhere. Not that chair though — that's George's chair!

translations.fa: در اول سمت چپ. هر جا خواستید بشینید. ولی اون صندلی نه — اون صندلی جورجه!

branches.suggestion: Where should I sit?
George has his own chair?

n6.speaker: tom
n6.text: Nobody sits in George's chair! House rule. The sofa's comfy. Make yourselves at home.

translations.fa: هیچ‌کس رو صندلی جورج نمی‌شینه! قانون خونه. مبل راحته. راحت باشید.

branches.suggestion: Thank you. Your house is lovely.
It's very warm in here.

n7.speaker: khan
n7.text: Thank you, Tom. It's very cosy. Is that William I can hear?

translations.fa: ممنون تام. خیلی دنجه. این صدای ویلیامه؟

branches.suggestion: I think he's awake.
He's singing!

cultureNote.en: British "cosy", American "cozy".
cultureNote.fa: cosy/cozy.

n8.speaker: tom
n8.text: Singing! That's my boy. Right, drinks. Tea, coffee, juice? I'll be back in a jiffy!

translations.fa: آواز! پسر خودمه. خب، نوشیدنی. چای، قهوه، آبمیوه؟ یه چشم به هم زدن برمی‌گردم!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Hello! Sorry, would you mind taking your shoes off? We've got a new carpet!

translations.fa: سلام! ببخشید، اشکالی نداره کفشاتون را دربیارید؟ فرش نو داریم!

branches.suggestion: Of course. No problem.
We always do that in Iran.
branches.suggestionFa: ما تو ایران همیشه این کار را می‌کنیم.

cultureNote.en: Some British homes ask guests to take shoes off; others don't. If you're not sure, ask "Shoes on or off?"
cultureNote.fa: کفش در خانه‌های بریتانیایی.

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: Really? Always? Tom thinks it's strange. He walks everywhere in his boots!

translations.fa: واقعاً؟ همیشه؟ تام فکر می‌کنه عجیبه. همه جا با چکمه‌هاش راه میره!

branches.suggestion: In Iran, it's very rude to wear shoes inside.
branches.suggestionFa: تو ایران پوشیدن کفش تو خونه خیلی بی‌ادبیه.

branches.suggestion: Shoes are dirty. Carpets are clean.

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: That makes sense. Persian carpets are famous! Here, would you like some slippers?

translations.fa: منطقیه. فرش ایرانی معروفه! بیا، دمپایی می‌خوای؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, please. My feet are cold.
No thanks. Socks are fine.

n4.speaker: khan
n4.text: Do you mind if I keep my shoes on, Leslie? My back is still bad. Bending is hard.

translations.fa: اشکالی نداره کفشم پام بمونه، لزلی؟ کمرم هنوز بده. خم شدن سخته.

branches.suggestion: Let me help you, Mrs Khan.
Sit down. I'll do it.

match: do you mind if i keeping
recasts.echo: Do I mind? Not at all!
recasts.better: Do you mind if I keep my shoes on?

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: Oh, of course not, Amina! Keep them on. The carpet will survive.

translations.fa: آه، معلومه که نه آمینا! بذار پات باشه. فرش طوریش نمیشه.

branches.suggestion: That's kind, Leslie.
Where shall I put my shoes?

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: On the rack by the door. Next to Ryan's smelly trainers. Sorry about those!

translations.fa: رو جاکفشی کنار در. کنار کتونی‌های بدبوی رایان. بابت اونا ببخشید!

branches.suggestion: Ha! They really are smelly.
I've seen worse!

cultureNote.en: British "trainers", American "sneakers".
cultureNote.fa: trainers/sneakers.

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Ha! Come through. Mind the toys on the floor — Nicola's been busy. Tea's nearly ready!

translations.fa: ها! بیاید تو. مواظب اسباب‌بازی‌های رو زمین باشید — نیکولا حسابی سرگرم بوده. چای تقریباً آماده‌ست!

n1.speaker: ryan
n1.text: Mum told me to be a good host. Would you like a biscuit?

translations.fa: مامان گفت میزبان خوبی باشم. بیسکویت میل دارید؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, please. Thank you.
What kind of biscuits are they?

n2.speaker: ryan
n2.text: Chocolate digestives, custard creams and rich tea. Help yourself!

translations.fa: دایجستیو شکلاتی، کاستارد کریم و ریچ تی. بفرمایید!

branches.suggestion: I'd like a chocolate one, please.
What's a custard cream?

cultureNote.en: Digestives, custard creams and rich tea are classic British biscuits, perfect with tea.
cultureNote.fa: بیسکویت‌های کلاسیک بریتانیایی.

match: i like a chocolate one please
recasts.echo: Would you like a chocolate one? Here you go!
recasts.better: I'd like a chocolate one, please.

n3.speaker: ryan
n3.text: Two biscuits with vanilla cream in the middle. Would you like a cup of tea with it?

translations.fa: دو تا بیسکویت با خامهٔ وانیلی وسطش. با چای میل دارید؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, please. With milk, no sugar.
branches.suggestionFa: آره، لطفاً. با شیر، بدون شکر.

branches.suggestion: Just water for me, thanks.

n4.speaker: khan
n4.text: Ryan, what a gentleman! Could I have a tea too, love? Milk and two sugars.

translations.fa: رایان، چه آقایی! منم یه چای می‌تونم بخورم عزیزم؟ با شیر و دو تا قند.

branches.suggestion: Two sugars! Sweet tooth!
Shall I help you, Ryan?

n5.speaker: ryan
n5.text: Nah, I've got it. Now, the most important question: are you a dunker?

translations.fa: نه، خودم می‌تونم. خب، مهم‌ترین سؤال: تو اهل فرو کردنی؟

branches.suggestion: What's a dunker?
Yes! I dunk everything.
branches.suggestionFa: آره! همه چی را فرو می‌کنم.

cultureNote.en: Dunking biscuits in tea is a much-loved (and much-argued-about) British habit.
cultureNote.fa: فرو کردن بیسکویت در چای.

n6.speaker: ryan
n6.text: You dunk your biscuit in your tea. But not too long, or it falls in! Try it.

translations.fa: بیسکویتت را تو چایت فرو می‌کنی. ولی نه زیاد، وگرنه می‌افته! امتحان کن.

branches.suggestion: Mmm, that's good!
Oh no, it fell in!

n7.speaker: ryan
n7.text: Ha! Biscuit soup. Happens to the best of us. Would you like another one?

translations.fa: ها! سوپ بیسکویت. برای بهترین‌ها هم پیش میاد. یکی دیگه میل دارید؟

branches.suggestion: No thanks, I'm full.
Just one more, please.

n8.speaker: ryan
n8.text: Take two. Dad will eat them all if you don't! Mum, I was a good host — can I go now?

translations.fa: دو تا بردار. اگه نخوری بابا همه را می‌خوره! مامان، میزبان خوبی بودم — حالا می‌تونم برم؟

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Are you off already? It's only nine o'clock!

translations.fa: دارید میرید؟ تازه ساعت نهه!

branches.suggestion: Yes, I've got work tomorrow.
It's late for Mrs Khan.

n2.speaker: khan
n2.text: I'm an old lady, Leslie! Nine is very late for me. Thank you for a lovely evening.

translations.fa: من یه پیرزنم لزلی! نه برای من خیلی دیره. ممنون بابت یه شب عالی.

branches.suggestion: Thank you for having us.
The food was delicious.

cultureNote.en: "Thanks for having me/us" is the standard British way to thank a host.
cultureNote.fa: Thanks for having us.

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: Thank you for coming! And for the samosas and the sweets. You must come again.

translations.fa: ممنون که اومدید! و بابت سمبوسه‌ها و شیرینی‌ها. باید دوباره بیاید.

branches.suggestion: We'd love to.
Next time, come to mine!

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: Yes! I want to try your Persian cooking. Wait — take some food home!

translations.fa: آره! می‌خوام آشپزی ایرانیت را امتحان کنم. صبر کنید — یه کم غذا ببرید خونه!

branches.suggestion: Oh no, that's too much.
Thank you. That's very kind.

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: There's loads! Here's a box for you, and one for Amina. Have you got your coats?

translations.fa: کلی هست! اینم یه جعبه برای تو، یکی هم برای آمینا. کتاتون را برداشتید؟

branches.suggestion: Yes. And my umbrella.
Where's my scarf?

recasts.echo: Thanks for having you? Any time!

n6.speaker: khan
n6.text: {you}, can you walk me home? It's only next door, but it's dark.

translations.fa: {you}، منو تا خونه می‌رسونی؟ همین بغله، ولی تاریکه.

branches.suggestion: Of course, Mrs Khan.
Take my arm.

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Night night! Text me when you're home safe. Ha — you both live next door! Bye!

translations.fa: شب بخیر! وقتی سالم رسیدید پیام بدید. ها — هر دوتون که بغل دستید! خداحافظ!

n1.speaker: weda
n1.text: Hello, dear! I'm running William's bath. Can you pass me his duck?

translations.fa: سلام عزیزم! دارم وان ویلیام را پر می‌کنم. اردکش را بهم میدی؟

branches.suggestion: Here's the duck.
Is the water too hot?

n2.speaker: weda
n2.text: Good question. I always check with my elbow. Like this. It's just right.

translations.fa: سؤال خوبیه. من همیشه با آرنجم امتحان می‌کنم. این‌جوری. درست اندازه‌ست.

branches.suggestion: With your elbow? Why?
Just right. Good.

cultureNote.en: An old British tip: test a child's bath with your elbow, which feels heat more than your hand.
cultureNote.fa: تست آب با آرنج.

n3.speaker: william
n3.text: Bath time! Splash, splash!

translations.fa: وقت حمومه! شالاپ، شالاپ!

branches.suggestion: He's splashing!
I'm getting wet!

n4.speaker: weda
n4.text: Ha! He's splashing everyone. Can you hand me the baby shampoo? The yellow bottle.

translations.fa: ها! داره رو همه آب می‌پاشه. شامپوی بچه را میدی؟ بطری زرده.

branches.suggestion: This one?
Here you are, Maggie.

recasts.echo: Here you are? Thank you, dear.

n5.speaker: weda
n5.text: Thank you, dear. Now I'm washing his hair. He hates this part. Sing something!

translations.fa: ممنون عزیزم. حالا دارم موهاش را می‌شورم. از این قسمت متنفره. یه چیزی بخون!

branches.suggestion: Twinkle, twinkle, little star…
branches.suggestionFa: چشمک بزن، چشمک بزن، ستارهٔ کوچولو…

branches.suggestion: The wheels on the bus go round and round!

n6.speaker: william
n6.text: The bus song! Sing it again!

translations.fa: آهنگ اتوبوس! دوباره بخون!

branches.suggestion: He loves that song.
Round and round!

n7.speaker: weda
n7.text: You're a star. All done! Now I'm getting the towel. Can you hold him? Careful, he's slippery!

translations.fa: تو ستاره‌ای. تموم شد! حالا دارم حوله را میارم. می‌تونی نگهش داری؟ مواظب باش، لیزه!

branches.suggestion: I'm holding him.
He's like a fish!

n8.speaker: weda
n8.text: Ha! A little fish. Wrap him up. Lovely. Now pyjamas and bed, little one. Say night night!

translations.fa: ها! یه ماهی کوچولو. بپیچش. عالی. حالا پیژامه و تخت، کوچولو. بگو شب بخیر!

n1.speaker: weda
n1.text: Oh, bother! Have you seen my slippers, dear? The pink fluffy ones.

translations.fa: ای بابا! دمپایی‌هام را دیدی عزیزم؟ صورتی پشمالوها.

branches.suggestion: No, I haven't. Where did you leave them?
Are they in the bathroom?

n2.speaker: weda
n2.text: I don't remember! My memory is terrible these days. Are they under the bath?

translations.fa: یادم نیست! این روزا حافظه‌م افتضاحه. زیر وانن؟

branches.suggestion: No, they aren't under the bath.
I can see one! Behind the door.

n3.speaker: weda
n3.text: One! Where's the other one? I can't walk with one slipper!

translations.fa: یکی! اون یکی کجاست؟ با یه دمپایی که نمی‌تونم راه برم!

branches.suggestion: Is it in your bedroom?
Maybe William has it.

n4.speaker: william
n4.text: That's mine! It's my shoe!

translations.fa: مال منه! کفش منه!

branches.suggestion: William! You have Nana's slipper!
It's not a shoe, it's a slipper!

n5.speaker: weda
n5.text: You cheeky monkey! Is he chewing it?

translations.fa: ای شیطون! داره می‌جوئدش؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, he's chewing it!
Give it to Nana, William.

cultureNote.en: "Cheeky monkey" is a loving British way to tell off a naughty child.
cultureNote.fa: cheeky monkey.

recasts.echo: He's chewing it? Oh dear!

n6.speaker: weda
n6.text: Thank you, dear. A bit wet, but never mind. Have you seen my glasses too?

translations.fa: ممنون عزیزم. یه کم خیسه، ولی عیب نداره. عینکم را هم دیدی؟

branches.suggestion: They're on your head, Maggie!
Where did you last have them?

n7.speaker: weda
n7.text: On my head! Oh, silly me. What would I do without you? You and William, my little helpers!

translations.fa: رو سرم! آه، چه حواس‌پرتی. بدون تو چی کار می‌کردم؟ تو و ویلیام، کمک‌کارهای کوچولوی من!

n1.speaker: weda
n1.text: Look what I found in the cupboard! My old photo album. Would you like to see?

translations.fa: ببین تو کمد چی پیدا کردم! آلبوم عکس قدیمیم. می‌خوای ببینی؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, please!
Are these very old?

n2.speaker: weda
n2.text: Very old! This is me. I was twenty. Wasn't I pretty?

translations.fa: خیلی قدیمی! این منم. بیست سالم بود. خوشگل نبودم؟

branches.suggestion: You were beautiful!
Where were you?

n3.speaker: weda
n3.text: I was in Brighton, at the seaside. And this is George. He was very handsome!

translations.fa: برایتون بودم، کنار دریا. و این جورجه. خیلی خوش‌تیپ بود!

branches.suggestion: Was George a porter then?
His hair was very black!

n4.speaker: weda
n4.text: Yes, he was a porter at Piccadilly station, in Manchester. And look — here's a little boy. Who is it?

translations.fa: آره، باربر ایستگاه پیکادلی منچستر بود. و ببین — اینم یه پسر کوچولو. کیه؟

branches.suggestion: Is that Tom?
Was it Ryan?

n5.speaker: weda
n5.text: It's Tom! He was five. He was very naughty. He was always on a bus, even then!

translations.fa: تامه! پنج سالش بود. خیلی شیطون بود. حتی اون موقع هم همیشه تو اتوبوس بود!

branches.suggestion: Ha! Tom was cute.
Were you happy then?

recasts.echo: Tom was naughty? Very!

n6.speaker: weda
n6.text: Very happy. Times were hard, but we were happy. Were your parents young in your photos?

translations.fa: خیلی خوشحال. اوضاع سخت بود، ولی خوشحال بودیم. پدر و مادرت تو عکس‌هات جوون بودن؟

branches.suggestion: Yes. My mum was very young.
My photos are on my phone!

n7.speaker: weda
n7.text: On your phone! Show me one, dear. I want to see your family. Is that your mum? She has kind eyes.

translations.fa: تو گوشیت! یکی نشونم بده عزیزم. می‌خوام خانواده‌ت را ببینم. این مامانته؟ چشمای مهربونی داره.

n1.speaker: weda
n1.text: William's asleep at last. Now it's time for us. Would you like a cup of tea, dear?

translations.fa: بالاخره ویلیام خوابید. حالا وقت ماست. یه فنجون چای میل داری عزیزم؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, please. I'd love one.
Let me make it, Maggie.

n2.speaker: weda
n2.text: No, no, sit down. You're my guest. How do you like your tea?

translations.fa: نه، نه، بشین. مهمون منی. چای را چطوری دوست داری؟

branches.suggestion: Strong, with a little milk.
No milk, please. Just black.

n3.speaker: weda
n3.text: Ooh, very Persian! Tom likes his tea "builder's" — very strong, two sugars.

translations.fa: اوه، خیلی ایرانی! تام چایش را «بنایی» دوست داره — خیلی پررنگ، دو تا قند.

branches.suggestion: What's builder's tea?
In Iran, we drink tea with sugar cubes.
branches.suggestionFa: تو ایران با قند چای می‌خوریم.

cultureNote.en: "Builder's tea" is strong black tea with milk and sugar — named after workers who drink lots of it.
cultureNote.fa: چای بنایی.

n4.speaker: weda
n4.text: Strong tea for hard workers! Would you like a slice of Victoria sponge? I made it this morning.

translations.fa: چای پررنگ برای آدم‌های سخت‌کوش! یه برش کیک ویکتوریا میل داری؟ امروز صبح پختمش.

branches.suggestion: Yes, please. Just a small piece.
branches.suggestionFa: آره، لطفاً. فقط یه تیکهٔ کوچیک.

branches.suggestion: No, thank you. I'm full.

match: yes please a small one piece
recasts.echo: A small piece? Here you are.
recasts.better: Yes, please. Just a small piece.
recasts.betterFa: آره، لطفاً. فقط یه تیکهٔ کوچیک.

n5.speaker: weda
n5.text: Full? Nonsense! A small piece never hurt anybody. Here. With jam and cream.

translations.fa: سیر؟ مزخرفه! یه تیکهٔ کوچیک به کسی آسیب نزده. بیا. با مربا و خامه.

branches.suggestion: Thank you. It's delicious!
This is the best cake ever.

cultureNote.en: British hosts often insist on cake — a polite "Just a small piece, then" usually works best!
cultureNote.fa: اصرار میزبان به کیک.

n6.speaker: weda
n6.text: Oh, you're a charmer! Would you like more tea? There's plenty in the pot.

translations.fa: آه، چه زبون‌بازی! چای بیشتر میل داری؟ تو قوری زیاده.

branches.suggestion: Yes, please. Just half a cup.
No more, thank you. That was perfect.

n7.speaker: weda
n7.text: This is nice. Just you, me and a pot of tea. George and I did this for fifty years!

translations.fa: چه خوبه. فقط تو، من و یه قوری چای. من و جورج پنجاه سال این کار را می‌کردیم!

n1.speaker: tom
n1.text: I'm home! I'm starving! What's for tea?

translations.fa: اومدم خونه! دارم از گشنگی می‌میرم! شام چیه؟

branches.suggestion: We're having spaghetti bolognese.
I don't know. Ask Leslie!

cultureNote.en: In much of Britain, "tea" can mean the evening meal; others say "dinner" or "supper".
cultureNote.fa: tea یعنی شام.

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: Spag bol! Ryan's favourite. It's ready in ten minutes. Can you lay the table, Tom?

translations.fa: اسپاگ بول! غذای محبوب رایان. ده دقیقه دیگه آماده‌ست. میز را می‌چینی تام؟

branches.suggestion: I'll help you, Tom.
What's spag bol?

n3.speaker: tom
n3.text: Short for spaghetti bolognese. We Brits shorten everything! How was your day, {you}?

translations.fa: کوتاه‌شدهٔ اسپاگتی بولونز. ما بریتانیایی‌ها همه چی را کوتاه می‌کنیم! روزت چطور بود {you}؟

branches.suggestion: It was good, thanks. Busy.
Tiring. I had my English class.

n4.speaker: tom
n4.text: English class! You're doing brilliantly. My day? A pigeon got on the bus. At the Angel!

translations.fa: کلاس انگلیسی! داری عالی پیش میری. روز من؟ یه کبوتر سوار اتوبوس شد. تو انجل!

branches.suggestion: A pigeon? What happened?
Did it pay?

n5.speaker: tom
n5.text: Ha! No, it didn't pay! It sat upstairs, at the front. Like you! Then it got off at Islington.

translations.fa: ها! نه، کرایه نداد! طبقهٔ بالا، جلو نشست. مثل تو! بعد تو ایزلینگتون پیاده شد.

branches.suggestion: That's so funny!
A very clever pigeon.

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: Tea's ready! Everyone sit down. Would you like parmesan, {you}?

translations.fa: شام آماده‌ست! همه بشینید. پارمزان می‌خوای {you}؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, please. Lots!
Just a little, thanks.

recasts.echo: Lots of cheese? Here you go!

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: I want lots too! And no green bits!

translations.fa: منم زیاد می‌خوام! و تیکه‌های سبز نه!

branches.suggestion: The green bits are herbs.
Green bits are good for you!

n8.speaker: tom
n8.text: Right. Phones away, everyone. Ryan, that means you! Now, who wants to hear about my pigeon?

translations.fa: خب. همه گوشی‌ها کنار. رایان، یعنی تو! حالا کی می‌خواد دربارهٔ کبوترم بشنوه؟

n1.speaker: ryan
n1.text: Dinner's done. Telly time! What shall we watch?

translations.fa: شام تموم شد. وقت تلویزیونه! چی ببینیم؟

branches.suggestion: Shall we watch the news?
Is there any football on?

cultureNote.en: "Telly" is informal British English for television. Americans say "TV".
cultureNote.fa: telly/TV.

n2.speaker: ryan
n2.text: The news? Boring! I'd rather watch football. Arsenal are playing.

translations.fa: اخبار؟ کسل‌کننده‌ست! ترجیح میدم فوتبال ببینم. آرسنال بازی داره.

branches.suggestion: OK. I'd rather watch football too.
branches.suggestionFa: باشه. منم ترجیح میدم فوتبال ببینم.

branches.suggestion: Who are they playing?

recasts.echo: You'd rather watch football? Same!

n3.speaker: ryan
n3.text: Spurs. Big game! But Nicola wants cartoons and Mum wants Bake Off.

translations.fa: اسپرز. بازی بزرگیه! ولی نیکولا کارتون می‌خواد و مامان بیک آف.

branches.suggestion: What's Bake Off?
Three different shows!

cultureNote.en: "The Great British Bake Off" is a very popular TV baking competition.
cultureNote.fa: مسابقهٔ آشپزی بیک آف.

n4.speaker: ryan
n4.text: A baking show. People make cakes in a tent and cry. Mum loves it. So what's the rule?

translations.fa: یه برنامهٔ شیرینی‌پزی. آدم‌ها تو یه چادر کیک می‌پزن و گریه می‌کنن. مامان عاشقشه. خب قانون چیه؟

branches.suggestion: Cartoons first, for Nicola.
We can watch the match on your phone.
branches.suggestionFa: می‌تونیم بازی را رو گوشیت ببینیم.

n5.speaker: ryan
n5.text: Good shout. Nicola's cartoon is only twenty minutes. Then Mum, then the match.

translations.fa: فکر خوبیه. کارتون نیکولا فقط بیست دقیقه‌ست. بعد مامان، بعد بازی.

branches.suggestion: But the match is at eight.
We can record it.

n6.speaker: ryan
n6.text: Record it! And no spoilers. If you see the score, don't tell me! Shall we get snacks?

translations.fa: ضبطش کنیم! و لو ندی. اگه نتیجه را دیدی، بهم نگو! خوراکی بیاریم؟

branches.suggestion: Crisps or popcorn?
I'd rather have fruit.

cultureNote.en: British "crisps", American "chips". British "chips" = American "fries".
cultureNote.fa: crisps/chips.

n7.speaker: ryan
n7.text: Fruit? Who are you, Mum? Crisps. Salt and vinegar. Right, remote's mine. Sit down — cartoons are starting!

translations.fa: میوه؟ تو کی هستی، مامان؟ چیپس. نمک و سرکه. خب، کنترل مال منه. بشین — کارتون داره شروع میشه!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Right, Nicola! Bath, pyjamas, teeth, story. In that order!

translations.fa: خب نیکولا! حموم، پیژامه، دندون، قصه. به همین ترتیب!

branches.suggestion: First a bath, Nicola.
That's a lot of jobs!

cultureNote.en: British "pyjamas", American "pajamas".
cultureNote.fa: pyjamas/pajamas.

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: But I had a bath yesterday! Can I skip the bath?

translations.fa: ولی دیروز حموم کردم! می‌شه حموم را نرم؟

branches.suggestion: No, sorry. Bath first.
A quick one, then.

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: A quick bath. Then which pyjamas? The unicorns or the stars?

translations.fa: یه حموم سریع. بعد کدوم پیژامه؟ تک‌شاخی یا ستاره‌ای؟

branches.suggestion: The unicorns!
Which ones do you like, Nicola?

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: The stars! Then after that, can I have milk?

translations.fa: ستاره‌ای! بعد از اون، می‌تونم شیر بخورم؟

branches.suggestion: First pyjamas, then milk.
After milk, you brush your teeth.
branches.suggestionFa: بعد از شیر، دندونات را مسواک می‌زنی.

recasts.echo: Pyjamas first, then milk? Yes!

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: Good. Then teeth for two minutes. Use the timer. Can you help her, {you}?

translations.fa: خوبه. بعد دو دقیقه مسواک. از تایمر استفاده کن. کمکش می‌کنی {you}؟

branches.suggestion: Sure. Where's her toothbrush?
Two minutes is a long time!

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: The pink one! It sings a song. When the song stops, I stop!

translations.fa: صورتیه! آهنگ می‌خونه. وقتی آهنگ تموم شد، منم تموم می‌کنم!

branches.suggestion: Up and down, Nicola.
Don't forget the back teeth!

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Lovely. Finally, story time and lights out. Who's reading tonight?

translations.fa: عالی. در آخر، وقت قصه و خاموش کردن چراغ. امشب کی می‌خونه؟

branches.suggestion: I can read tonight.
Nicola, choose a book.

n8.speaker: nicola
n8.text: {you}! {you}! Tell me a story from Iran! Not a book. A real story!

translations.fa: {you}! {you}! برام یه قصه از ایران بگو! نه کتاب. یه قصهٔ واقعی!

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: I'm in bed! Mr Buttons is here too. Tell me a story from Iran! Please!

translations.fa: تو تختم! آقای دکمه هم اینجاست. یه قصه از ایران بگو! لطفاً!

branches.suggestion: Once upon a time, there was a big bird.
branches.suggestionFa: یکی بود یکی نبود، یه پرندهٔ بزرگ بود.

branches.suggestion: OK. Do you want a story about a king?
branches.suggestionFa: باشه. یه قصه دربارهٔ یه پادشاه می‌خوای؟

newWords.fa: روزی روزگاری ؛ یکی بود یکی نبود

cultureNote.en: Persian stories often start "Yeki bood, yeki nabood" — "One was, one wasn't" — like "Once upon a time".
cultureNote.fa: یکی بود یکی نبود.

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: A big bird! How big? Bigger than a bus?

translations.fa: یه پرندهٔ بزرگ! چقدر بزرگ؟ بزرگ‌تر از اتوبوس؟

branches.suggestion: Bigger than a house! Her name was Simorgh.
branches.suggestionFa: بزرگ‌تر از یه خونه! اسمش سیمرغ بود.

branches.suggestion: She was as big as a mountain!

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: Simorgh! Where did she live?

translations.fa: سیمرغ! کجا زندگی می‌کرد؟

branches.suggestion: She lived on top of a high mountain.
branches.suggestionFa: بالای یه کوه بلند زندگی می‌کرد.

branches.suggestion: In a nest in a magic tree.
branches.suggestionFa: تو یه لونه رو یه درخت جادویی.

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: Ooh. Was she kind or scary?

translations.fa: اوه. مهربون بود یا ترسناک؟

branches.suggestion: She was very kind and very wise.
branches.suggestionFa: خیلی مهربون و خیلی دانا بود.

branches.suggestion: She was kind, but she was scary to bad people!
branches.suggestionFa: مهربون بود، ولی برای آدم‌های بد ترسناک بود!

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: What did she do?

translations.fa: چی کار کرد؟

branches.suggestion: One day, she found a little baby boy.
branches.suggestionFa: یه روز، یه پسر بچه پیدا کرد.

branches.suggestion: She saved a baby on the mountain.
branches.suggestionFa: یه بچه را رو کوه نجات داد.

recasts.echo: She found a baby? Then what?

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: A baby! Like William was? Did she look after him?

translations.fa: یه بچه! مثل ویلیام وقتی کوچیک بود؟ ازش مراقبت کرد؟

branches.suggestion: Yes. She looked after him for years.
She gave him food and kept him warm.
branches.suggestionFa: بهش غذا داد و گرمش نگه داشت.

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: Like Nana looks after William! Then what happened? Did he grow up?

translations.fa: مثل نانا که از ویلیام مراقبت می‌کنه! بعد چی شد؟ بزرگ شد؟

branches.suggestion: He grew up and became a hero.
Shh. That's for tomorrow night!

n8.speaker: nicola
n8.text: Tomorrow night?! OK… Simorgh is my favourite now. Night night, {you}. Night night, Simorgh…

translations.fa: فردا شب؟! باشه… الان سیمرغ محبوب منه. شب بخیر {you}. شب بخیر سیمرغ…

n1.speaker: ellis
n1.text: Thank you for volunteering! Every visitor needs a badge. What's your name?

translations.fa: ممنون که داوطلب شدید! هر بازدیدکننده‌ای کارت لازم داره. اسمتون چیه؟

branches.suggestion: My name is {you}.
I'm Nicola's neighbour, {you}.

cultureNote.en: UK schools always ask visitors to sign in and wear a badge, for the children's safety.
cultureNote.fa: ثبت ورود و کارت بازدیدکننده.

n2.speaker: ellis
n2.text: Lovely. And how do you spell that?

translations.fa: عالی. و چطوری هجی میشه؟

branches.suggestion: Can I write it for you?
I'll spell it slowly.

n3.speaker: ellis
n3.text: Yes, slowly, please. My hearing isn't great with all these children!

translations.fa: آره، آروم لطفاً. با این همه بچه گوشم خوب نمی‌شنوه!

branches.suggestion: Is it M or N? It's M.
M for mother.

cultureNote.en: To make spelling clear, people say "M for mother", "B for bus", etc.
cultureNote.fa: M for mother برای وضوح.

n4.speaker: ellis
n4.text: M for mother, perfect. Is that with a double letter?

translations.fa: M مثل مادر، عالی. حرف دوتایی داره؟

branches.suggestion: No, just one of each.
Yes, two E's.

recasts.echo: Two E's? Thank you!

n5.speaker: ellis
n5.text: Thank you. And your surname? We need it for the signing-in book.

translations.fa: ممنون. و نام خانوادگیتون؟ برای دفتر ثبت ورود لازمه.

branches.suggestion: It's quite long. Shall I write it?
Shall I spell my surname?

n6.speaker: ellis
n6.text: Write it here, please. Oh, that's a beautiful name. How do you say it?

translations.fa: لطفاً اینجا بنویسیدش. آه، چه اسم قشنگی. چطوری تلفظش می‌کنید؟

branches.suggestion: Let me say it slowly for you.
Most people get it wrong!

n7.speaker: ellis
n7.text: I'll practise! Here's your badge. The children will call you "Mr" and your first name.

translations.fa: تمرین می‌کنم! اینم کارتتون. بچه‌ها شما را «آقای» به اضافهٔ اسم کوچیکتون صدا می‌کنن.

branches.suggestion: That's fine.
Do the children call you Mrs Ellis?
branches.suggestionFa: بچه‌ها شما را خانم الیس صدا می‌کنن؟

n8.speaker: ellis
n8.text: Yes, or just "Miss"! Now, come and meet the children. They're very excited!

translations.fa: آره، یا فقط «میس»! حالا بیاید بچه‌ها را ببینید. خیلی هیجان‌زده‌ان!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: The kids call me "Mrs Thompson" at school. It's funny — I was "Miss Parker" before I married Tom!

translations.fa: بچه‌ها تو مدرسه منو «خانم تامپسون» صدا می‌کنن. خنده‌داره — قبل از ازدواج با تام «دوشیزه پارکر» بودم!

branches.suggestion: Did you change your surname?
What's the difference between Miss and Mrs?

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: "Miss" is for a woman who isn't married. "Mrs" is for a married woman. And "Ms" is for anyone.

translations.fa: «میس» برای زن مجرده. «میسز» برای زن متأهل. و «میز» برای همه.

branches.suggestion: So Ms is easier!
And men are always "Mr"?

cultureNote.en: Many British women use "Ms" because it doesn't show if they are married.
cultureNote.fa: Ms بدون اشاره به تأهل.

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: Yes! Men are lucky. Always "Mr". Did your mum change her name when she married?

translations.fa: آره! مردها خوش‌شانسن. همیشه «مستر». مامانت وقتی ازدواج کرد اسمش را عوض کرد؟

branches.suggestion: No. In Iran, women keep their surname.
branches.suggestionFa: نه. تو ایران زن‌ها نام خانوادگیشون را نگه می‌دارن.

branches.suggestion: No, she kept her family name.
branches.suggestionFa: نه، نام خانوادگی خودش را نگه داشت.

recasts.echo: She kept her name? Interesting!

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: Really? I like that. Lots of women here keep their names now too. Some use both!

translations.fa: واقعاً؟ خوشم میاد. الان اینجا هم خیلی از زن‌ها اسمشون را نگه می‌دارن. بعضی هر دو را استفاده می‌کنن!

branches.suggestion: Both names? Like a double surname?
branches.suggestionFa: هر دو اسم؟ مثل یه نام خانوادگی دوتایی؟

branches.suggestion: What about the children?

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: Yes, with a hyphen. Like "Parker-Thompson". Our kids are just Thompson. What's your middle name?

translations.fa: آره، با خط تیره. مثل «پارکر-تامپسون». بچه‌های ما فقط تامپسونن. اسم وسطت چیه؟

branches.suggestion: I don't have a middle name.
What's a middle name?

cultureNote.en: Many British people have a middle name, often from a grandparent.
cultureNote.fa: نام میانی از پدربزرگ یا مادربزرگ.

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: A second first name! Mine is Rose, after my nan. Nicola's is Margaret, after Nana Maggie!

translations.fa: یه اسم کوچیک دوم! مال من رُزه، به اسم مادربزرگم. مال نیکولا مارگارته، به اسم نانا!

branches.suggestion: That's lovely. Nicola Margaret Thompson.
Does Ryan have a middle name?

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Ryan George Thompson. After Grandad. Don't tell him I told you — he says "George" is an old man's name!

translations.fa: رایان جورج تامپسون. به اسم پدربزرگ. نگی بهت گفتم — میگه «جورج» اسم پیرمرداست!

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Look! I can write my name! N-I-C-O-L-A. Is it right?

translations.fa: ببین! می‌تونم اسمم را بنویسم! ان-آی-سی-او-ال-ای. درسته؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, it's perfect!
Nearly! Use a capital N.
branches.suggestionFa: تقریباً! از N بزرگ استفاده کن.

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: Mrs Ellis says names start with a big letter. Big N, then small letters.

translations.fa: خانم الیس میگه اسم‌ها با حرف بزرگ شروع میشن. N بزرگ، بعد حروف کوچیک.

branches.suggestion: That's right. Capital N.
And small i, c, o, l, a.
branches.suggestionFa: و i، c، o، l، a کوچیک.

cultureNote.en: Teachers in England say "capital letters" and "lower-case" or "small letters".
cultureNote.fa: capital/lower-case.

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: Now can I write YOUR name? How do I start?

translations.fa: حالا می‌تونم اسم تو را بنویسم؟ چطوری شروع کنم؟

branches.suggestion: With a capital letter!
I'll write it, and you copy it.
branches.suggestionFa: من می‌نویسمش، تو ازش رونویسی کن.

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: OK. Ooh, it's hard. Can you write it in Persian too?

translations.fa: باشه. اوه، سخته. می‌تونی به فارسی هم بنویسیش؟

branches.suggestion: Sure. Persian goes from right to left.
branches.suggestionFa: حتماً. فارسی از راست به چپ نوشته میشه.

branches.suggestion: Here it is in Persian.

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Right to left! Backwards! Is there a capital letter in Persian?

translations.fa: از راست به چپ! برعکس! تو فارسی حرف بزرگ هست؟

branches.suggestion: No, there are no capital letters.
But letters change shape!

recasts.echo: There are no capital letters? Wow!

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: No capitals?! Lucky! Can you write MY name in Persian?

translations.fa: حرف بزرگ نداره؟! خوش به حالشون! می‌تونی اسم منو به فارسی بنویسی؟

branches.suggestion: Here's Nicola in Persian.
It looks like this.

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: It's so pretty! Like a little snake and dots! I'm going to show Mrs Ellis!

translations.fa: خیلی قشنگه! مثل یه مار کوچولو و نقطه! می‌خوام به خانم الیس نشونش بدم!

n1.speaker: ellis
n1.text: In Reception, we learn letter sounds first. Not names. "A" is "a" for apple. Do you know phonics?

translations.fa: تو کلاس آمادگی، اول صدای حروف را یاد می‌گیریم. نه اسمشون را. «ای» میشه «اَ» مثل اپل. فونیکس بلدید؟

branches.suggestion: What's phonics?
I learnt letter names first.
branches.suggestionFa: من اول اسم حروف را یاد گرفتم.

cultureNote.en: Children in England learn to read with "phonics" — the sounds letters make, not their names.
cultureNote.fa: آموزش خواندن با فونیکس.

n2.speaker: ellis
n2.text: It's how children learn to read. "C-A-T" — c, a, t — "cat"! Let's try. What's this word?

translations.fa: این‌جوری بچه‌ها خوندن یاد می‌گیرن. «سی-ای-تی» — ک، اَ، ت — «کت»! بیاید امتحان کنیم. این کلمه چیه؟

branches.suggestion: D-O-G. Dog!
Is it "dog"?

n3.speaker: ellis
n3.text: Brilliant! You're a natural. Now, the tricky one. How do you say the last letter of the alphabet?

translations.fa: عالی! استعدادش را دارید. حالا یکی سخت. آخرین حرف الفبا را چطوری میگید؟

branches.suggestion: Zed.
Zee?

cultureNote.en: The British say "zed" for Z; Americans say "zee".
cultureNote.fa: zed/zee.

n4.speaker: ellis
n4.text: "Zed" here! "Zee" is American. The children love songs. Do you know the alphabet song?

translations.fa: اینجا «زِد»! «زی» آمریکاییه. بچه‌ها عاشق آهنگن. آهنگ الفبا را بلدید؟

branches.suggestion: Yes. A, B, C, D…
No. Can you teach me?

n5.speaker: ellis
n5.text: Lovely. Now, how many letters are there in the English alphabet?

translations.fa: عالی. حالا الفبای انگلیسی چند تا حرف داره؟

branches.suggestion: There are twenty-six letters.
branches.suggestionFa: بیست و شش تا حرف داره.

branches.suggestion: Twenty-six. Persian has thirty-two!
branches.suggestionFa: بیست و شش. فارسی سی و دو تا داره!

recasts.echo: Twenty-six letters? Correct!
recasts.betterFa: بیست و شش تا حرف داره.

n6.speaker: ellis
n6.text: Thirty-two! Wow. Which letter is the hardest in English for you?

translations.fa: سی و دو! وای. کدوم حرف انگلیسی برات سخت‌تره؟

branches.suggestion: W. It's hard to say.
The "th" sound. It's not in Persian.

n7.speaker: ellis
n7.text: "Th" is hard for lots of people. Tongue between your teeth: "Th-ank you". Perfect!

translations.fa: «ث» برای خیلی‌ها سخته. زبون بین دندون‌ها: «ثنک یو». عالی!

n1.speaker: ryan
n1.text: Chips for tea! Best night of the week. Do you like chips?

translations.fa: شام چیپس! بهترین شب هفته. سیب‌زمینی سرخ‌کرده دوست داری؟

branches.suggestion: I love chips!
I don't mind them.

cultureNote.en: "I don't mind" means "it's OK for me" — not strong like or dislike.
cultureNote.fa: I don't mind یعنی برایم فرقی ندارد.

n2.speaker: ryan
n2.text: Don't mind? They're the best! Ketchup or mayo? Big question.

translations.fa: فرقی نمی‌کنه؟ بهترینن! کچاپ یا مایونز؟ سؤال مهم.

branches.suggestion: Ketchup, please.
I like mayo better.

n3.speaker: ryan
n3.text: Mayo! Like the Belgians. I like both. But Dad hates mayo!

translations.fa: مایونز! مثل بلژیکی‌ها. من هر دو را دوست دارم. ولی بابا از مایونز متنفره!

branches.suggestion: Why does Tom hate mayo?
branches.suggestionFa: چرا تام از مایونز بدش میاد؟

branches.suggestion: I hate ketchup on everything.
branches.suggestionFa: من از کچاپ رو همه چی متنفرم.

recasts.echo: Tom hates mayo? It's true!

n4.speaker: ryan
n4.text: He says it's "too wobbly". Weird. Do you like vinegar on your chips?

translations.fa: میگه «زیادی لرزونه». عجیبه. سرکه رو چیپست دوست داری؟

branches.suggestion: Vinegar on chips? Really?
I don't like vinegar. It's sour.

cultureNote.en: Salt and vinegar on chips is a classic British combination.
cultureNote.fa: نمک و سرکه روی چیپس.

n5.speaker: ryan
n5.text: It's amazing! Try one. Salt and vinegar. Go on!

translations.fa: فوق‌العاده‌ست! یکی امتحان کن. نمک و سرکه. یالا!

branches.suggestion: Mmm! I like it!
No, I really don't like it.

n6.speaker: ryan
n6.text: Your face! Ha! What about gravy? Northerners love chips with gravy.

translations.fa: صورتت! ها! گریوی چطور؟ شمالی‌ها عاشق چیپس با گریوی‌ان.

branches.suggestion: Gravy on chips? I'd like to try that.
branches.suggestionFa: گریوی رو چیپس؟ دوست دارم امتحانش کنم.

branches.suggestion: I don't like gravy.

cultureNote.en: In the North of England, "chips and gravy" is popular; in Scotland, chips with "salt and sauce".
cultureNote.fa: چیپس و گریوی در شمال.

n7.speaker: ryan
n7.text: Fair enough. More for me! Pass the chips. Last one's mine!

translations.fa: حق داری. بیشتر برای من! چیپس‌ها را بده. آخریش مال منه!

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Yuck! There are mushrooms in my pasta! I don't like mushrooms!

translations.fa: اَه! تو پاستام قارچه! قارچ دوست ندارم!

branches.suggestion: Have you tried them?
Just eat around them.

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: I tried them once. They're slimy. Like slugs! Do you like mushrooms?

translations.fa: یه بار امتحان کردم. لزجن. مثل حلزون بی‌صدف! تو قارچ دوست داری؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, I like mushrooms a lot.
I like them, but not in pasta.
branches.suggestionFa: دوستشون دارم، ولی نه تو پاستا.

recasts.echo: You like mushrooms? Lots of people do!

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: Then you can have mine! Here! What don't you like?

translations.fa: پس مال منو بخور! بیا! تو چی دوست نداری؟

branches.suggestion: I don't like spicy food.
I don't like olives.

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: Olives! They're yucky too! Mummy likes olives. And Daddy doesn't like sprouts.

translations.fa: زیتون! اونم بده! مامان زیتون دوست داره. و بابا کلم بروکسل دوست نداره.

branches.suggestion: What are sprouts?
Nobody likes sprouts!

cultureNote.en: Brussels sprouts are a famous Christmas vegetable — and Britain's most argued-about one!
cultureNote.fa: کلم بروکسل در کریسمس.

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Little green balls. Like tiny cabbages. They smell like socks!

translations.fa: توپ‌های کوچیک سبز. مثل کلم‌های کوچولو. بوی جوراب میدن!

branches.suggestion: Ha! Socks!
They're good with butter.

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: Nicola, two mushrooms, then you can have pudding. Deal?

translations.fa: نیکولا، دو تا قارچ، بعد می‌تونی دسر بخوری. قبول؟

branches.suggestion: That's fair, Nicola.
Two small ones!

cultureNote.en: British people often say "pudding" or "pud" for any dessert.
cultureNote.fa: pudding یعنی دسر.

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: Two tiny ones… Mmm. OK, they're not slugs. But I still don't like them. What's for pudding?

translations.fa: دو تا کوچولو… ممم. باشه، حلزون نیستن. ولی هنوز دوستشون ندارم. دسر چیه؟

n1.speaker: tom
n1.text: Question for the table! What's everyone's favourite food? Mine is a Sunday roast!

translations.fa: سؤال برای همه! غذای محبوب همه چیه؟ مال من کباب یکشنبه‌ست!

branches.suggestion: What's a Sunday roast?
Mine is ghormeh sabzi.

cultureNote.en: A Sunday roast is roast meat, roast potatoes, vegetables, Yorkshire pudding and gravy — a British tradition.
cultureNote.fa: ناهار سنتی یکشنبه.

n2.speaker: tom
n2.text: Roast beef, roast potatoes, Yorkshire puddings, gravy… Heaven! What's yours, {you}?

translations.fa: رست‌بیف، سیب‌زمینی تنوری، یورکشایر پودینگ، گریوی… بهشت! مال تو چیه {you}؟

branches.suggestion: My favourite is ghormeh sabzi.
I love kebab with rice.

match: my favourite is the kebab rice
recasts.echo: Your favourite is kebab with rice? Yum!
recasts.better: My favourite is kebab with rice.

n3.speaker: tom
n3.text: Ghormeh… sabzi? What's in it?

translations.fa: قورمه… سبزی؟ توش چیه؟

branches.suggestion: It's a stew with herbs, beans and lamb.
branches.suggestionFa: یه خورش با سبزی، لوبیا و گوشت برّه‌ست.

branches.suggestion: Lots of green herbs and dried lemons.

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: It sounds delicious! My favourite is Indian. A chicken tikka masala.

translations.fa: خوشمزه به نظر میاد! محبوب من هندیه. چیکن تیکا ماسالا.

branches.suggestion: I like curry too.
Is that British food?

cultureNote.en: Chicken tikka masala is often called one of Britain's favourite dishes, though it comes from British-Indian cooking.
cultureNote.fa: تیکا ماسالا غذای محبوب بریتانیایی.

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: My favourite is fish fingers! With ketchup! And Mr Buttons likes honey.

translations.fa: محبوب من فیش فینگره! با کچاپ! و آقای دکمه عسل دوست داره.

branches.suggestion: Like Winnie the Pooh!
Good choice, Nicola.

n6.speaker: ryan
n6.text: Pizza. Obviously. And William's favourite is… everything on the floor!

translations.fa: پیتزا. معلومه. و محبوب ویلیام… همه چی که رو زمینه!

branches.suggestion: Ha! What's your favourite pudding, Tom?
William likes bananas.

n7.speaker: tom
n7.text: Sticky toffee pudding with custard! OK, decision made. {you}, will you cook ghormeh sabzi for us one day?

translations.fa: پودینگ تافی چسبناک با کاستارد! خب، تصمیم گرفته شد. {you}، یه روز برامون قورمه‌سبزی درست می‌کنی؟

branches.suggestion: Yes! Next Sunday.
Only if you make a Sunday roast for me!
branches.suggestionFa: فقط اگه تو برام کباب یکشنبه درست کنی!

n8.speaker: tom
n8.text: Deal! Roast one week, ghormeh sabzi the next. Best neighbours in Hackney!

translations.fa: قبول! یه هفته کباب، هفتهٔ بعد قورمه‌سبزی. بهترین همسایه‌های هکنی!

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Psst! {you}! I'll give you my carrots if you give me your roast potato. Swap?

translations.fa: پیس! {you}! هویجم را بهت میدم اگه سیب‌زمینیت را بهم بدی. عوض کنیم؟

branches.suggestion: No way! I love roast potatoes!
Hmm. Two carrots for one potato?
branches.suggestionFa: هوم. دو تا هویج برای یه سیب‌زمینی؟

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: Three carrots! Three! That's a good swap!

translations.fa: سه تا هویج! سه تا! معاملهٔ خوبیه!

branches.suggestion: It's not fair. You don't like carrots!
branches.suggestionFa: منصفانه نیست. تو که هویج دوست نداری!

branches.suggestion: OK, three carrots. Deal!

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: Nicola! I can see you. No swapping. Eat your own carrots, please.

translations.fa: نیکولا! دارم می‌بینمت. معامله ممنوع. لطفاً هویج خودت را بخور.

branches.suggestion: Sorry, Leslie!
It was her idea!

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: But Mummy… carrots are boring. Can I swap with Mr Buttons?

translations.fa: ولی مامان… هویج کسل‌کننده‌ست. می‌تونم با آقای دکمه عوض کنم؟

branches.suggestion: Mr Buttons doesn't eat carrots!
Teddies don't eat, Nicola.

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: Eat four carrots and you can have pudding. If you don't, no pudding.

translations.fa: چهار تا هویج بخور، اون وقت دسر داری. اگه نخوری، دسر نداری.

branches.suggestion: Four carrots, then pudding.
What's for pudding?

match: if you eat carrot you have pudding
recasts.echo: If you eat your carrots, you can have pudding? Exactly!
recasts.better: If you eat your carrots, you can have pudding.
recasts.betterFa: اگه هویجت را بخوری، دسر داری.

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: What's for pudding? If it's ice cream, I'll eat five carrots!

translations.fa: دسر چیه؟ اگه بستنی باشه، پنج تا هویج می‌خورم!

branches.suggestion: It's apple crumble!
Five carrots! Good girl!

cultureNote.en: Apple crumble with custard is a classic British pudding.
cultureNote.fa: کرامبل سیب.

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Apple crumble AND ice cream. So five carrots, please. Starting… now!

translations.fa: کرامبل سیب و بستنی. پس پنج تا هویج، لطفاً. از… الان!

branches.suggestion: Go, Nicola, go!
I'm counting! One… two…

n8.speaker: nicola
n8.text: Done! Five carrots! I'm a carrot champion! Can I have the biggest bowl, please?

translations.fa: تموم شد! پنج تا هویج! من قهرمان هویجم! می‌تونم بزرگ‌ترین کاسه را بگیرم، لطفاً؟

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Atchoo! Oh, I feel awful. My nose is running and my throat is sore.

translations.fa: هاپچه! آه، حالم افتضاحه. آبریزش بینی دارم و گلوم درد می‌کنه.

branches.suggestion: Bless you! You've got a cold.
You look really tired.

cultureNote.en: British people often say they're "under the weather" when they feel a bit ill.
cultureNote.fa: under the weather یعنی کمی کسالت.

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: But I've got thirty children waiting for me! Should I go to school?

translations.fa: ولی سی تا بچه منتظرمن! برم مدرسه؟

branches.suggestion: No, you shouldn't. Stay at home.
Have you got a temperature?

n3.speaker: leslie
n3.text: A little bit. Thirty-seven point eight. But the Year 4s have a test today!

translations.fa: یه کم. سی و هفت و هشت دهم. ولی کلاس چهارمی‌ها امروز امتحان دارن!

branches.suggestion: You should call the school.
Another teacher can do the test.
branches.suggestionFa: یه معلم دیگه می‌تونه امتحان بگیره.

recasts.echo: You should call the school? You're right.

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: You're right. I'll call in sick. I hate it, though. I feel so guilty!

translations.fa: راست میگی. زنگ می‌زنم مرخصی استعلاجی می‌گیرم. ولی ازش متنفرم. خیلی عذاب وجدان دارم!

branches.suggestion: You shouldn't feel guilty.
Everyone gets ill sometimes.

cultureNote.en: In the UK, you can take up to seven days off sick without a doctor's note ("self-certification").
cultureNote.fa: تا هفت روز بدون گواهی پزشک.

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: True. And I shouldn't give my cold to the kids. What should I do now?

translations.fa: درسته. و نباید سرماخوردگیم را به بچه‌ها بدم. حالا چی کار کنم؟

branches.suggestion: You should go back to bed.
You should drink lots of water.

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: Bed sounds lovely. But who takes Nicola to school? Tom's on the early shift.

translations.fa: تخت عالیه. ولی کی نیکولا را می‌بره مدرسه؟ تام شیفت صبحه.

branches.suggestion: I can take her.
Can Maggie take her?

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: You're an angel! Her book bag is by the door. And don't come too close — you'll get ill too!

translations.fa: فرشته‌ای! کیف کتابش کنار دره. و خیلی نزدیک نیا — تو هم مریض میشی!

n1.speaker: weda
n1.text: Oh dear. Nicola's got a tummy ache. She's on the sofa. Can you sit with her?

translations.fa: ای وای. نیکولا دل‌درد داره. رو مبله. می‌تونی پیشش بشینی؟

branches.suggestion: Of course. What's wrong, Nicola?
Poor Nicola. What happened?

cultureNote.en: "Tummy" is a gentle, childish word for stomach.
cultureNote.fa: tummy واژهٔ کودکانهٔ شکم.

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: My tummy hurts! Ow!

translations.fa: دلم درد می‌کنه! آخ!

branches.suggestion: Where does it hurt?
Does it hurt a lot?

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: Here. In the middle. It's all wobbly.

translations.fa: اینجا. وسطش. همه‌ش قار و قور می‌کنه.

branches.suggestion: What did you eat today?
Did you eat lots of sweets?

n4.speaker: weda
n4.text: That's the question! Somebody found the party bags. All ten of them!

translations.fa: سؤال همینه! یکی کیسه‌های جشن را پیدا کرده. همهٔ ده تاش را!

branches.suggestion: Ten party bags?!
Oh, Nicola! The jelly snakes!

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Only five… or six. Sorry, Nana. Will I be OK?

translations.fa: فقط پنج تا… یا شیش تا. ببخشید نانا. خوب میشم؟

branches.suggestion: Yes, you'll be fine.
You need to rest now.

recasts.echo: You'll be fine? Yes, you will!

n6.speaker: weda
n6.text: You'll be fine, pet. Small sips of water. And no more sweets today!

translations.fa: خوب میشی عزیزم. آب جرعه جرعه. و امروز دیگه آبنبات نه!

branches.suggestion: Here's some water, Nicola.
Do you want a blanket?

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: Yes please. The fluffy one. Can you stroke my tummy? Nana does it in circles.

translations.fa: آره لطفاً. پشمالوئه. می‌تونی شکمم را نوازش کنی؟ نانا دایره‌ای این کار را می‌کنه.

branches.suggestion: Like this? In circles?
Is it a bit better now?

n8.speaker: nicola
n8.text: A bit better. I don't want ANY sweets. Never again! … Well, maybe next week.

translations.fa: یه کم بهتره. هیچ آبنباتی نمی‌خوام. دیگه هیچ‌وقت! … خب، شاید هفتهٔ بعد.

n1.speaker: weda
n1.text: Brrr! It's a chilly night. My old bones are cold. Could you fill my hot water bottle, dear?

translations.fa: بررر! شب سردیه. استخونای پیرم سرده. می‌شه کیسهٔ آب گرمم را پر کنی عزیزم؟

branches.suggestion: Of course. Where is it?
What's a hot water bottle?

cultureNote.en: Many British homes use a rubber hot water bottle to warm the bed on cold nights.
cultureNote.fa: کیسهٔ آب گرم رایج است.

n2.speaker: weda
n2.text: It's a rubber bag. You fill it with hot water. This one, with the knitted cover.

translations.fa: یه کیسهٔ لاستیکیه. با آب داغ پرش می‌کنی. همین که روکش بافتنی داره.

branches.suggestion: Did you knit the cover?
Shall I boil the kettle?

n3.speaker: weda
n3.text: Yes, I knitted it! Boil the kettle, but don't use boiling water. Let it cool a bit first.

translations.fa: آره، خودم بافتمش! کتری را جوش بیار، ولی از آب جوش استفاده نکن. اول بذار یه کم خنک بشه.

branches.suggestion: Why not boiling water?
OK. I'll wait two minutes.

n4.speaker: weda
n4.text: Boiling water can damage the rubber. And be careful — don't fill it to the top!

translations.fa: آب جوش لاستیک را خراب می‌کنه. و مواظب باش — تا بالا پرش نکن!

branches.suggestion: How much water?
Half full?

recasts.echo: Don't fill it to the top? Right!
recasts.better: Don't fill it to the top.

n5.speaker: weda
n5.text: About two-thirds full. Then squeeze out the air and screw the top on tight.

translations.fa: حدود دو سوم. بعد هواش را فشار بده بیرون و درش را محکم ببند.

branches.suggestion: Squeeze the air out. Done.
branches.suggestionFa: هوا را بیرون دادم. تموم شد.

branches.suggestion: Is the top tight enough?

n6.speaker: weda
n6.text: Let me check. Perfect! Ooh, lovely and warm. Don't put it on bare skin, it can burn.

translations.fa: بذار ببینم. عالی! اوه، گرم و خوب. رو پوست لخت نذار، ممکنه بسوزونه.

branches.suggestion: That's why it has a cover.
Here you are, Maggie.

n7.speaker: weda
n7.text: Clever you! Thank you, dear. Do you want one too? There's a spare one with a sheep on it.

translations.fa: آفرین به تو! ممنون عزیزم. تو هم یکی می‌خوای؟ یه یدکی هست که روش گوسفنده.

branches.suggestion: Yes, please! My room is cold.
No thanks. I've got a thick duvet.

n8.speaker: weda
n8.text: Take the sheep. Your landlord never puts the heating on, I know! Night night, dear. Sleep tight!

translations.fa: گوسفنده را ببر. می‌دونم صاحبخونه‌ت هیچ‌وقت شوفاژ را روشن نمی‌کنه! شب بخیر عزیزم. خوب بخوابی!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Good news! William's feeling better. Look at him!

translations.fa: خبر خوب! حال ویلیام بهتره. نگاش کن!

branches.suggestion: He's smiling again!
Is his temperature down?

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: Yes! Thirty-six point nine. Normal. He was so hot yesterday.

translations.fa: آره! سی و شش و نه دهم. نرماله. دیروز خیلی داغ بود.

branches.suggestion: He's much better than yesterday.
That's a relief!

recasts.echo: He's better than yesterday? Much!

n3.speaker: william
n3.text: Can we play ball now?

translations.fa: الان می‌تونیم توپ‌بازی کنیم؟

branches.suggestion: He wants to play!
Here's your ball, William.

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: He wants to play — that's always a good sign. Is he eating more? Let's try a banana.

translations.fa: می‌خواد بازی کنه — این همیشه نشونهٔ خوبیه. بیشتر می‌خوره؟ بیا یه موز امتحان کنیم.

branches.suggestion: Here's a banana.
He ate a little last night.

n5.speaker: william
n5.text: Nana! More banana, please!

translations.fa: نانا! موز بیشتر، لطفاً!

branches.suggestion: He wants more!
He's eating again!

n6.speaker: leslie
n6.text: More banana! Brilliant. He's eating better too. And you, {you}? Is your cold better or worse?

translations.fa: موز بیشتر! عالی. بهتر هم می‌خوره. و تو {you}؟ سرماخوردگیت بهتره یا بدتر؟

branches.suggestion: It's better, thanks.
A bit worse today.

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: Oh no — I gave it to you! I'm so sorry. Do you want some of William's banana? Ha!

translations.fa: ای وای — من بهت دادمش! خیلی ببخشید. یه کم از موز ویلیام می‌خوای؟ ها!

branches.suggestion: No thanks. Tea is better!
Ha! Little kids get better faster than adults.
branches.suggestionFa: ها! بچه‌های کوچیک از بزرگ‌ترها زودتر خوب میشن.

n8.speaker: leslie
n8.text: That's true! Tomorrow he can go back to pre-school. And you can go back to bed. Doctor's orders!

translations.fa: راسته! فردا می‌تونه برگرده پیش‌دبستانی. و تو می‌تونی برگردی تو تخت. دستور دکتر!

n1.speaker: nicola
n1.text: Oops! I spilled my juice! It's everywhere! Sorry! Sorry!

translations.fa: اوه! آبمیوه‌م را ریختم! همه جا ریخت! ببخشید! ببخشید!

branches.suggestion: Don't worry. It's only juice.
Oh dear! Let's clean it up.

cultureNote.en: British people often write "spilt"; Americans write "spilled". Both are fine.
cultureNote.fa: spilt/spilled.

n2.speaker: nicola
n2.text: It's on the table and on the floor. And on Mr Buttons!

translations.fa: رو میز و رو زمینه. و رو آقای دکمه!

branches.suggestion: Where's a cloth?
Poor Mr Buttons!

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: The kitchen roll is by the sink. Can I help?

translations.fa: دستمال کاغذی کنار سینکه. می‌تونم کمک کنم؟

branches.suggestion: Yes. You wipe the table.
branches.suggestionFa: آره. تو میز را پاک کن.

branches.suggestion: Hold the cup, please.

cultureNote.en: British "kitchen roll", American "paper towels".
cultureNote.fa: kitchen roll/paper towels.

n4.speaker: nicola
n4.text: I'm wiping! How did it happen? I knocked it with my elbow!

translations.fa: دارم پاک می‌کنم! چطوری شد؟ با آرنجم زدمش!

branches.suggestion: Accidents happen.
Be careful with your elbows!

recasts.echo: You knocked it with your elbow? That happens!
recasts.better: You knocked it with your elbow.

n5.speaker: nicola
n5.text: Now the floor is sticky! My socks are sticking! Ew!

translations.fa: حالا زمین چسبناکه! جورابام دارن می‌چسبن! اَه!

branches.suggestion: Let's mop the floor.
Take your socks off.

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: What about Mr Buttons? Is he OK? He smells like apple!

translations.fa: آقای دکمه چی؟ خوبه؟ بوی سیب میده!

branches.suggestion: He needs a bath!
We can wash him in the machine.

n7.speaker: nicola
n7.text: In the washing machine?! Will he be dizzy? OK… but a gentle wash!

translations.fa: تو ماشین لباسشویی؟! سرش گیج نمیره؟ باشه… ولی شستشوی ملایم!

n1.speaker: leslie
n1.text: Oh no! Nicola fell over in the garden. Her knee is bleeding. Can you get the first aid kit?

translations.fa: ای وای! نیکولا تو حیاط افتاد. زانوش داره خون میاد. می‌تونی جعبهٔ کمک‌های اولیه را بیاری؟

branches.suggestion: Yes! Where is it?
Is she OK?

n2.speaker: leslie
n2.text: In the top cupboard, the green box. Nicola, sweetie, let me see.

translations.fa: تو کابینت بالایی، جعبهٔ سبز. نیکولا، عزیزم، بذار ببینم.

branches.suggestion: Here's the green box.
It's only a little graze.

n3.speaker: nicola
n3.text: It hurts! It's got stones in it! Waaah!

translations.fa: درد می‌کنه! توش سنگریزه‌ست! واااای!

branches.suggestion: You're very brave, Nicola.
It's OK. Mummy's here.

n4.speaker: leslie
n4.text: First, we wash it with water. Can you pass me the wipes?

translations.fa: اول با آب می‌شوریمش. دستمال‌های مرطوب را میدی؟

branches.suggestion: Here are the wipes.
Will it sting?

n5.speaker: leslie
n5.text: It might sting a little. Be brave, Nicola. One, two, three… done!

translations.fa: شاید یه کم بسوزه. شجاع باش نیکولا. یک، دو، سه… تموم شد!

branches.suggestion: Well done! All clean.
That wasn't so bad!

recasts.echo: It might sting? Just a little.

n6.speaker: nicola
n6.text: Can I have a plaster? A dinosaur one!

translations.fa: می‌تونم چسب زخم بزنم؟ یه دایناسوری!

branches.suggestion: Here's a dinosaur plaster.
Which dinosaur do you want?

cultureNote.en: British "plaster", American "Band-Aid".
cultureNote.fa: plaster/Band-Aid.

n7.speaker: leslie
n7.text: There. Now a kiss to make it better. Better?

translations.fa: ایناهاش. حالا یه بوس که خوب بشه. بهتر شد؟

branches.suggestion: Do you feel better now?
Big hug, Nicola!

n8.speaker: nicola
n8.text: Better. Can I have a biscuit? Biscuits make knees better too!

translations.fa: بهتر. می‌تونم یه بیسکویت بخورم؟ بیسکویت زانو را هم خوب می‌کنه!

branches.suggestion: Ha! Nice try!
Ask Mummy!

n9.speaker: leslie
n9.text: Just one, for being so brave. And no more running on the patio, OK? Walk, don't run!

translations.fa: فقط یکی، برای این‌همه شجاعت. و دیگه رو پاسیو ندو، باشه؟ راه برو، ندو!

n1.speaker: ryan
n1.text: Oh no, no, no! I broke Mum's favourite mug! The one with the cats!

translations.fa: ای وای، نه، نه! ماگ محبوب مامان را شکستم! اونی که گربه‌ها داره!

branches.suggestion: Oh dear! How did it happen?
Don't touch it! It's sharp.

n2.speaker: ryan
n2.text: It slipped out of my hand. It was an accident! She's going to kill me!

translations.fa: از دستم لیز خورد. اتفاقی بود! منو می‌کشه!

branches.suggestion: She won't kill you!
Just tell her the truth.

n3.speaker: ryan
n3.text: First, help me pick it up. Careful. Get the dustpan and brush.
